title: Cyclic data, trace budget, and support size
label: def:cyclic-data-trace-budget
statement: A countable cyclic datum is a family \[ \mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}, \qquad n_j,m_j\in\NN,\quad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\}, \] indexed by a finite or countably infinite set \(J\). Its trace budget, formal positive determinant, and numerical support size are \[ \tau_{\mathcal D} :=\sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}\in[0,\infty], \] \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z) :=\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j}, \qquad N_{\mathcal D}:=\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\in\NN\cup\{\infty\}. \] When \(J\) is infinite this product notation is formal until a theorem imposes a convergence hypothesis. In every analytic determinant identity below it means the locally uniform limit, on compact subsets of \(\CC\), of the finite subproducts directed by \(F\Subset J\). Thus a displayed infinite product is never used as an unordered pointwise product without its finite-subset convergence convention. The associated cyclic zero divisor is the divisor on \(\CC^\times\) \[ Z_{\mathcal D} :=\sum_{j\in J}m_j\sum_{\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j}[\lambda]. \] Thus a point \(\lambda\in\CC^\times\) has divisor multiplicity \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) :=\sum_{\{j\in J:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}}m_j, \] possibly \(+\infty\) before summability or realisability hypotheses are imposed. Equivalently, the factor \((1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j}\) contributes multiplicity \(m_j\) at every root \(\lambda\) of \(\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\). The symbol \(N_{\mathcal D}\) is a count of cyclic spectral slots. When \(J\) is infinite it is used only as the statement that there are infinitely many such slots; the Hilbert-space dimension of the closed support of the associated separable cyclic model is then \(\aleph_0\), not the extended integer \(\infty\). If \(\tau_{\mathcal D}<\infty\), choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\) and set \[ H_{\mathcal D} :=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(\CC^{n_j}\otimes\CC^{m_j}\bigr), \qquad L_{\mathcal D} :=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\bigr). \]

title: Single cyclic-block spectrum
label: lem:single-cyclic-block-spectrum
statement: Let \(n,m\in\NN\), \(\beta\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\), and \(\alpha^n=\beta\). Then the non-zero eigenvalues of \(C(n,\alpha)\otimes I_m\) are \[ \alpha\omega,\qquad \omega^n=1, \] each with multiplicity \(m\), and \[ \det\!\bigl(I-z(C(n,\alpha)\otimes I_m)\bigr) =(1-\beta z^n)^m . \]

title: Finite cyclic truncation determinant with positive exponents
label: lem:finite-cyclic-truncation-determinant
statement: Let \(F\) be a finite set of indices and put \[ L_F:=\bigoplus_{j\in F}\bigl(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\bigr), \qquad \alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j. \] Then, as a finite-dimensional determinant identity, \[ \det(I-zL_F) =\prod_{j\in F}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j}, \qquad \det(I-zL_F)^{-1} =\prod_{j\in F}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{-m_j} \] wherever the reciprocal is defined.

title: Direct normal convergence of the cyclic product
label: lem:direct-cyclic-weierstrass-product
statement: Assume \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty, \qquad a_j:=\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}. \] Then for every \(R>0\), \[ \sum_{j\in J} m_j \sup_{\abs z\le R}\abs{\beta_j z^{n_j}} \le \sum_{j\in J}m_j\abs{\beta_j}R^{n_j} =\sum_{j\in J}m_j(Ra_j)^{n_j} <\infty. \] Consequently the infinite product \[ \prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] converges normally on compact subsets of \(\CC\). In particular it converges locally uniformly, defines an entire function, and its value is independent of the enumeration of \(J\).

title: Trace-norm limit convention for cyclic products
label: lem:cyclic-product-trace-norm-limit
statement: Assume \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty \] and choose \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\). Let \[ H_{\mathcal D} :=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(\CC^{n_j}\otimes\CC^{m_j}\bigr), \qquad L_{\mathcal D} :=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\bigr) \] on \(H_{\mathcal D}\), and let \(L_{\mathcal D}^{(N)}\) be any finite truncation along an enumeration of \(J\). Then \(L_{\mathcal D}^{(N)}\to L_{\mathcal D}\) in trace norm and \[ \prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} =\lim_{N\to\infty} \prod_{j\le N}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] locally uniformly for \(z\in\CC\), and \[ \det(I-zL_{\mathcal D}) =\lim_{N\to\infty} \prod_{j\le N}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] locally uniformly for \(z\in\CC\). On any connected zero-free neighbourhood \(\Omega\ni0\) for this determinant, \[ \det(I-zL_{\mathcal D})^{-1} =\lim_{N\to\infty} \prod_{j\le N}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{-m_j} \] locally uniformly on \(\Omega\). Thus the negative-exponent product is used only as the reciprocal of the non-vanishing Fredholm determinant on such a domain.

title: Choice of roots and unitary relabelling
label: lem:choice-of-roots
statement: Let \(n,m\in\NN\), let \(\beta\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\), and let \(\alpha^n=(\alpha')^n=\beta\). Then \(C(n,\alpha)\otimes I_m\) and \(C(n,\alpha')\otimes I_m\) are unitarily equivalent. More explicitly, if \(\eta:=\alpha'/\alpha\), so that \(\eta^n=1\), and \((e_0,\dots,e_{n-1})\) is the cyclic basis in which \(\Pi_n e_k=e_{k+1\!\!\pmod n}\), then \[ U_\eta e_k:=\eta^k e_k \qquad (0\le k<n) \] defines a unitary on \(\CC^n\) satisfying \[ U_\eta C(n,\alpha)U_\eta^{-1}=C(n,\alpha'). \] Consequently any two root choices in the construction of \(L_{\mathcal D}\) give unitarily equivalent cyclic models, via the block direct sum of the maps \(U_{\eta_j}\otimes I_{m_j}\). The determinant data therefore determine the cyclic model only up to this explicit relabelling and the addition of zero summands.

title: Cyclic construction interface for cyclic data
label: prop:cyclic-data-construction-interface
statement: Let \(\mathcal D\) be a countable cyclic datum in the sense of \Cref{def:cyclic-data-trace-budget} with \(\tau_{\mathcal D}<\infty\), and choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\). For each finite \(F\Subset J\), set \[ H_F:=\bigoplus_{j\in F}(\CC^{n_j}\otimes\CC^{m_j}), \qquad L_F:=\bigoplus_{j\in F}(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}), \] and regard \(L_F\) as acting by zero on the orthogonal complement of \(H_F\) in \(H_{\mathcal D}\). Then the net \((L_F)_{F\Subset J}\), directed by inclusion, converges unconditionally in trace norm to a normal operator \(L_{\mathcal D}\in\sone(H_{\mathcal D})\). This limit satisfies \[ \norm{L_{\mathcal D}}_1=\tau_{\mathcal D}, \qquad \dim H_{\mathcal D}= \begin{cases} N_{\mathcal D},& J\text{ finite},\\ \aleph_0,& J\text{ infinite}, \end{cases} \] where the second equality is a Hilbert-space dimension identity. Moreover \(D_{\mathcal D}\) is an entire function and \[ \det(I-zL_{\mathcal D})=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \] locally uniformly for \(z\in\CC\). The unitary equivalence class of \(L_{\mathcal D}\) is independent of the chosen roots; more precisely, replacing \(\alpha_j\) by another root \(\alpha_j'\) conjugates the \(j\)-th block by the diagonal relabelling from \(\Cref{lem:choice-of-roots}\), and the orthogonal direct sum of these relabellings conjugates the two cyclic models.

title: Closed non-zero spectral support
label: def:closed-nonzero-support
statement: For a normal trace-class operator \(L\), write \[ \mathsf S(L):= \overline{\mathrm{span}} \{\,\ker(L-\lambda I):\lambda\in\spec(L)\setminus\{0\}\,\}. \] This notation is the support convention used throughout the normal construction and classification sections; the model-specific range formula is recorded later in \Cref{lem:cyclic-sum-range-closure}.

title: Closed support is \(\overline{\Ran L}\)
label: lem:normal-support-range-closure
statement: If \(L\) is normal and trace-class, then \[ \mathsf S(L)=(\ker L)^\perp=\overline{\Ran(L)}. \] This identifies the closed support with \(\overline{\Ran L}\). It does not assert that \(\Ran L\) is closed.

title: Sharp trace-norm budget for cyclic zero divisors
label: prop:sharp-trace-budget-support-obstruction
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be a countable family with \(n_j,m_j\in\NN\) and \(\beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\). Choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\), and let \[ \Lambda_{\mathcal D} := \bigl\{\!\bigl\{\alpha_j\omega: j\in J,\ \omega^{n_j}=1,\text{ repeated }m_j\text{ times} \bigr\}\!\bigr\} \] be the prescribed non-zero spectral multiset, with multiplicities added when the same complex number occurs more than once. Suppose \(L\in\sone(H)\) is normal and its non-zero spectrum, counted with algebraic multiplicity, is exactly \(\Lambda_{\mathcal D}\). Then the trace-norm budget is forced: \[ \|L\|_1 = \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal D}}\abs{\lambda} = \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j} <\infty . \] Moreover \[ \dim \mathsf S(L)= \begin{cases} N_{\mathcal D},& J\text{ finite},\\ \aleph_0,& J\text{ infinite}, \end{cases} \] as a Hilbert-space dimension; equivalently, the finite numerical support count is \(N_{\mathcal D}=\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\) when \(J\) is finite, while a countably infinite datum gives separable infinite support dimension. If \(J\) is infinite, then \(\Ran L\) is a proper dense subspace of its closed support: \[ \Ran(L)\subsetneq \mathsf S(L) =\overline{\Ran(L)} . \] Conversely, when the displayed budget is finite, the cyclic direct sum \(L_{\mathcal D}\) supplied by \Cref{prop:cyclic-data-construction-interface}, with trace-norm control from \Cref{lem:cyclic-product-trace-norm-limit}, attains exactly this trace norm and this closed support.

title: Collapsed spectral multiplicities of Euler data
label: prop:collapsed-spectral-multiplicities
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ n_j,m_j\in\NN,\qquad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\},\qquad \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty, \] and choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\). For each \(\lambda\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\), define the collapsed multiplicity \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) :=\sum_{\{j\in J:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}} m_j. \] Then each \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\) is finite, the support \[ \Sigma_{\mathcal D} :=\{\lambda\in\CC\setminus\{0\}:M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\neq 0\} \] is countable, and for the cyclic model \[ L_{\mathcal D} =\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\bigr) \] one has \[ \dim\ker(L_{\mathcal D}-\lambda I)=M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) \qquad (\lambda\in\CC\setminus\{0\}). \] Consequently, \[ L_{\mathcal D} \cong \bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \lambda I_{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)}, \] and \[ \det(I-zL_{\mathcal D}) =\prod_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} (1-\lambda z)^{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)} \] as an entire function, where the right-hand side is the locally uniform limit of the corresponding finite products. Equivalently, the multiset \(\Lambda_{\mathcal D}\) of non-zero eigenvalues is exactly the multiset in which \(\lambda\) appears with multiplicity \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\). This is a collapse statement: it does not reconstruct the chosen Euler packaging \((n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\) from the determinant without auxiliary presentation data.

title: Regularized determinant normalization
label: def:regularized-determinant-normalization
statement: For an integer \(r\ge1\) and a finite-dimensional operator \(A\), this paper uses \[ \det_r(I-zA) := \det(I-zA) \exp\!\left(\sum_{q=1}^{r-1}\frac{z^q}{q}\operatorname{tr}(A^q)\right), \] with the empty sum interpreted as \(0\) when \(r=1\). This is the sign convention corresponding to \(\det_r(I+A)=\det(I+A)\exp(\sum_{q=1}^{r-1}(-1)^q\operatorname{tr}(A^q)/q)\) applied to \(A=-zT\), equivalently \(\det_r(I-T)=\det(I-T)\exp(\operatorname{tr}\sum_{q=1}^{r-1}T^q/q)\) in the normalization of \cite[Chapter~9]{Simon2005TraceIdeals} and \cite[eq.~(1.3)]{BritzCareyGesztesyNicholsSukochevZanin2021}.

title: Regularized determinant extension and cyclic-block factor
label: lem:regularized-determinant-extension-cyclic-factor
statement: The normalization of \Cref{def:regularized-determinant-normalization} extends to \(A\in\mathcal S_r\) as the standard regularized Fredholm determinant of order \(r\). It is the locally uniform limit, along finite-rank approximants converging in \(\mathcal S_r\), of the finite-rank expression in \Cref{def:regularized-determinant-normalization}; in particular, if \(T_n\to T\) in \(\mathcal S_r\), then \(\det_r(I-zT_n)\to\det_r(I-zT)\) locally uniformly in \(z\). Moreover \(\det_1(I-zA)=\det(I-zA)\) on trace-class operators, and for a finite cyclic block satisfying \(B^n=\beta I\), \[ \det_r(I-zB) =(1-\beta z^n) \exp\!\left(\sum_{1\le q\le (r-1)/n} \frac{\beta^q z^{qn}}{q}\right). \]

title: Regularized zero-divisor chain for cyclic blocks
label: prop:regularized-zero-divisor-chain
statement: Let \(r\ge1\), let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty \] for some \(1<p\le r\). This hypothesis is a prescribed cyclic \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget hypothesis, not merely the natural \(\mathcal S_r\)-domain condition for \(\det_r\). Let \(P_F^{(r)}\) be the finite-subset products determined by \Cref{lem:regularized-determinant-extension-cyclic-factor}. Then, for every finite \(F\Subset J\), the zero divisor of \(P_F^{(r)} \) on \(\CC\) is \[ \sum_{j\in F}m_j\sum_{\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j}[\lambda^{-1}], \] and the locally uniform limit supplied by \Cref{lem:regularized-cyclic-finite-subset-products} has finite zero order at \(z=\lambda^{-1}\) equal to \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) =\sum_{\{j\in J:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}}m_j \] for every \(\lambda\in\CC^\times\). Consequently, for the cyclic model \(L_{\mathcal D}\), the normalization of \Cref{def:regularized-determinant-normalization} changes only the zero-free entire factor in the determinant formula; the regularized determinant \(\det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal D})\) and the ordinary Fredholm determinant in the trace-class case have the same prescribed non-zero cyclic zero divisor.

title: Finite-subset convention for regularized cyclic products
label: lem:regularized-cyclic-finite-subset-products
statement: Let \(1<p\le r\) with \(r\in\NN\), and let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty. \] For \(F\Subset J\), define \[ P_F^{(r)}(z):= \prod_{j\in F}(1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j} \exp\!\left( m_j\sum_{1\le q\le (r-1)/n_j} \frac{\beta_j^qz^{qn_j}}{q} \right). \] Then \(P_F^{(r)}\) converges locally uniformly on \(\CC\), as \(F\Subset J\), to an entire function independent of the enumeration of \(J\). More precisely, for every \(R>0\), all but finitely many indices satisfy \(R\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}\le1/2\), and for such \(j\) and \(\abs z\le R\), \[ \left| \log\!\left[ (1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j} \exp\!\left( m_j\sum_{1\le q\le (r-1)/n_j} \frac{\beta_j^qz^{qn_j}}{q} \right) \right] \right| \le C_{p,r,R}\,m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}. \]

title: Exact Schatten membership threshold for the cyclic model
label: thm:schatten-cyclic-model-membership
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be countable cyclic data. The integer \(r\) is recorded only for the later regularized determinant statement; the present theorem classifies membership of the cyclic model in the smaller class \(\mathcal S_p\), not existence or uniqueness of \(\det_r\) on its natural domain \(\mathcal S_r\). Choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\), and form the cyclic direct sum \(L_{\mathcal D}=\bigoplus_j(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j})\) whenever it is defined as a compact operator. Then \[ L_{\mathcal D}\in\mathcal S_p \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty, \] and in this case \[ \norm{L_{\mathcal D}}_p^p =\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}. \]

title: Regularized cyclic determinant on a prescribed \(\mathcal S_p\) budget
label: thm:schatten-cyclic-regularized-determinant
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be countable cyclic data. Set \[ \tau_{\mathcal D,p} :=\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}\in[0,\infty]. \] This is a prescribed cyclic-data theorem in the smaller class \(\mathcal S_p\); its positive realization and rigidity content are exactly the finite-budget assertions \(\tau_{\mathcal D,p}<\infty\). It does not classify all regularized determinant fibers in the natural \(\mathcal S_r\)-domain. If \(\tau_{\mathcal D,p}<\infty\), choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\), and let \(L_{\mathcal D}\) be the cyclic model from \Cref{thm:schatten-cyclic-model-membership}. Then the finite-subset regularized cyclic products \(P_F^{(r)}\) from \Cref{lem:regularized-cyclic-finite-subset-products} converge locally uniformly on \(\CC\), independently of the enumeration of \(J\), to \[ \det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal D}) = \prod_{j\in J} (1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j} \exp\!\left( m_j\sum_{1\le q\le (r-1)/n_j} \frac{\beta_j^qz^{qn_j}}{q} \right). \] Equivalently, if \(p\) is an integer, this is the sharp \(\det_p\)-formula \[ \det_p(I-zL_{\mathcal D}) = \prod_{j\in J} (1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j} \exp\!\left( m_j\sum_{1\le q\le (p-1)/n_j} \frac{\beta_j^qz^{qn_j}}{q} \right). \] Conversely, if \(T\in\mathcal S_p(H)\) and the finite products on the right-hand side above, directed by finite subsets of \(J\), converge locally uniformly to \(\det_r(I-zT)\), then \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j} \le \norm{T}_p^p. \] Thus the displayed Schatten budget is the exact threshold for \(\mathcal S_p\)-membership of the normal cyclic model and the sharp lower bound in the prescribed cyclic-product regularized determinant problem attached to \(\mathcal D\). This is a prescribed-budget statement; it is not a classification of existence of \(\det_r\) on its full natural domain \(\mathcal S_r\).

title: Prescribed-budget regularized cyclic determinant
label: cor:regularized-controlled-extension-scope
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D\) be countable cyclic data satisfying \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty . \] Then the regularized product formula of \Cref{thm:schatten-cyclic-regularized-determinant} is a controlled extension of the trace-class Fredholm determinant realization theorem in the following precise sense. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item It first asserts the smaller-budget membership \(L_{\mathcal D}\in\mathcal S_p\) and computes \(\det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal D})\) for that model. \item Its converse lower bound applies only to operators \(T\in\mathcal S_p\) whose regularized determinant is obtained as the locally uniform prescribed cyclic product limit appearing in the theorem. \item It does not assert that every operator in the natural \(\mathcal S_r\)-domain of \(\det_r\), or every possible \(\det_r\)-zero divisor in that domain, is classified by the \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget. \end{enumerate}

title: Regularized determinant domain boundary
label: prop:regularized-domain-boundary
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D\) be cyclic data satisfying \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty . \] The conclusions of \Cref{thm:schatten-cyclic-regularized-determinant} are conclusions in the smaller Schatten class \(\mathcal S_p\): they give membership of the normal cyclic model in \(\mathcal S_p\), the explicit \(\det_r\)-factorization for that model, and the sharp lower bound for \(\mathcal S_p\)-operators whose regularized determinant has the prescribed cyclic product limit. They do not classify all operators in the natural determinant domain \(\mathcal S_r\), nor all \(\det_r\)-fibers with the same zero divisor but no prescribed cyclic product presentation. The only role of the larger natural domain here is to mark the boundary of the prescribed-budget theorem. More precisely, whenever \(p<r\) there are cyclic data for which \[ \sum_jm_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{r/n_j}<\infty, \qquad \sum_jm_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}=\infty . \] For those data the normal cyclic model belongs to \(\mathcal S_r\), and hence has a well-defined \(\det_r\), but it is not in \(\mathcal S_p\) and is outside the \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget theorem.

title: Classical ordered Weyl--Ky Fan--Lidskii inequality
label: lem:weyl-ky-fan-trace-class
statement: Let \(T\in\sone(H)\). Let \((\lambda_k(T))_{k\ge1}\) be the eigenvalues of \(T\), repeated according to algebraic multiplicity and ordered so that \[ \abs{\lambda_1(T)}\ge \abs{\lambda_2(T)}\ge \cdots, \] padding by zeros once the non-zero spectrum is exhausted. Let \((s_k(T))_{k\ge1}\) be the singular values of \(T\), ordered so that \[ s_1(T)\ge s_2(T)\ge \cdots \ge 0. \] Then for every \(N\ge1\), \[ \sum_{k=1}^N \abs{\lambda_k(T)} \le \sum_{k=1}^N s_k(T). \] Consequently, \[ \sum_{k\ge1}\abs{\lambda_k(T)}\le \|T\|_1. \]

title: Classical Schatten \texorpdfstring{\(p\)}{p}-sum Weyl--Fan inequality
label: lem:weyl-fan-schatten-p-sum
statement: Let \(0<p<\infty\) and let \(T\in\mathcal S_p(H)\). Let \((\lambda_k(T))_{k\ge1}\) be the eigenvalues of \(T\), repeated according to algebraic multiplicity, ordered by non-increasing modulus, and padded by zeros. Let \((s_k(T))_{k\ge1}\) be the singular values in non-increasing order. Then, for every \(N\ge1\), \[ \sum_{k=1}^N\abs{\lambda_k(T)}^p \le \sum_{k=1}^N s_k(T)^p, \] and consequently \[ \sum_{k\ge1}\abs{\lambda_k(T)}^p\le \norm{T}_p^p . \]

title: Ordered non-zero root-space flag
label: lem:ordered-nonzero-root-flag
statement: Let \(K\) be a compact operator on a separable Hilbert space, and let \((\mu_q)_{q\in Q}\), where \(Q=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) or \(Q=\NN\), be any ordering of the non-zero eigenvalues of \(K\), each repeated according to algebraic multiplicity. Then there is an increasing family \[ 0=E_0\subset E_1\subset E_2\subset\cdots \] of finite-dimensional \(K\)-invariant subspaces, indexed by \(q\in Q\), such that \(\dim E_q=q\) and the induced operator on \(E_q/E_{q-1}\) is multiplication by \(\mu_q\). If \(E:=\overline{\bigcup_q E_q}\), then \(E\) contains every non-zero Riesz root space of \(K\), and the compact operator induced by \(K\) on the quotient space \(H/E\) has no non-zero eigenvalues.

title: Classical Ringrose triangularisation in Schatten ideals
label: lem:ringrose-prescribed-diagonal
statement: Let \(1\le p<\infty\) and let \(T\in\mathcal S_p(H)\). After replacing \(H\) by the reducing subspace \[ H_T:=\overline{\mathrm{span}}\{u_r,v_r:r\ge1\} \] coming from any singular-value expansion \(T=\sum_{r\ge1}s_r(T)\langle\,\cdot\,,u_r\rangle v_r\), the operator acts on a separable Hilbert space and vanishes on \(H_T^\perp\). On this separable reducing part there is an orthonormal basis \((e_k)_{k\ge1}\) in which the matrix of \(T\) is upper triangular. The non-zero diagonal entries may be chosen so that their non-zero subsequence occurs in any prescribed ordering of the non-zero eigenvalues of \(T\), each repeated according to algebraic multiplicity. Every other diagonal entry is zero. Equivalently, the diagonal sequence \((d_k)_{k\ge1}\) has non-zero subsequence equal to the prescribed ordering of the non-zero algebraic eigenvalue multiset of \(T\), and all entries outside that subsequence are zero. This assertion imports Ringrose only for compact triangularisation on the separable reducing part; the prescribed ordering of non-zero diagonal entries is supplied by the finite-dimensional Riesz root-space flag in the proof below. It does not prescribe the positions occupied by zero entries, nor does it classify any quasinilpotent part at the spectral point \(0\). In particular, \[ \sum_{k\ge1}\abs{d_k}^p = \sum_{\lambda\in\spec(T)\setminus\{0\}} \abs{\lambda}^p\,m_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda) <\infty . \]

title: Two-by-two trace-norm pinching identity
label: lem:two-by-two-trace-norm-pinching
statement: For \(a,b,c\in\CC\), let \[ B=\begin{pmatrix}a&c\\0&b\end{pmatrix}. \] Then \[ \|B\|_1^2=(\abs{a}+\abs{b})^2+\abs{c}^2. \] In particular, \[ \|B\|_1\ge \abs{a}+\abs{b}, \] and equality holds if and only if \(c=0\).

title: Two-by-two Schatten pinching rigidity
label: lem:two-by-two-schatten-pinching
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\). For \(a,b,c\in\CC\), put \[ B=\begin{pmatrix}a&c\\0&b\end{pmatrix} \] and define \[ \Phi_p(a,b,c):=\|B\|_p^p-\abs a^p-\abs b^p . \] Then \[ \Phi_p(a,b,c)\ge0, \] Equality holds if and only if \(c=0\). For fixed \(a,b\), if \[ \Phi_p(a,b,c_\nu)\longrightarrow0, \] then \(c_\nu\to0\).

title: Uniform two-by-two Schatten pinching modulus
label: lem:uniform-two-by-two-schatten-modulus
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(E\subset\CC\) be finite, and let \(R>0\). For \(a,b,c\in\CC\), set \[ B(a,b,c):=\begin{pmatrix}a&c\\0&b\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \Phi_p(a,b,c):=\|B(a,b,c)\|_p^p-\abs a^p-\abs b^p . \] Define \[ \Theta_{p,E,R}(\varepsilon) := \sup\{\abs c: a,b\in E, \|B(a,b,c)\|_p\le R, \Phi_p(a,b,c)\le\varepsilon\}, \] with the convention that the supremum of the empty set is \(0\). Then \(\Theta_{p,E,R}\) is a finite nondecreasing function on \([0,\infty)\) and \[ \Theta_{p,E,R}(\varepsilon)\downarrow0 \qquad(\varepsilon\downarrow0). \] Consequently, whenever \(a,b\in E\), \(\|B(a,b,c)\|_p\le R\), and \(\Phi_p(a,b,c)\le\varepsilon\), one has \(\abs c\le\Theta_{p,E,R}(\varepsilon)\).

title: Standard trace-norm convergence of Schur compressions
label: lem:trace-norm-schur-compressions
statement: Let \(T\in\sone(H)\), and let \((P_N)_{N\ge1}\) be finite-rank orthogonal projections with \(P_N\to I\) strongly. Then \[ P_NTP_N\longrightarrow T \qquad\text{in }\sone\text{-norm}. \]

title: Standard Schatten-norm convergence of Schur compressions
label: lem:schatten-schur-compressions
statement: Let \(1\le p<\infty\), let \(T\in\mathcal S_p(H)\), and let \((P_N)_{N\ge1}\) be finite-rank orthogonal projections with \(P_N\to I\) strongly. Then \[ P_NTP_N\longrightarrow T \qquad\text{in }\mathcal S_p\text{-norm}. \]

title: Spectral rigidity for regularized determinants
label: lem:regularized-determinant-spectral-rigidity
statement: Let \(1\le r<\infty\), and let \(T_1,T_2\in\mathcal S_r\). If \[ \det_r(I-zT_1)=\det_r(I-zT_2) \] as entire functions, then the non-zero spectra of \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) coincide with algebraic multiplicity.

title: Zero-sector Schur elimination in an equality fiber
label: lem:zero-sector-schur-elimination-equality-fiber
statement: Let \(T\in\sone(H)\), and suppose that \[ \|T\|_1= \sum_{\lambda\in\sigma(T)\setminus\{0\}} \abs{\lambda}\,m_a(\lambda), \] where \(m_a(\lambda)\) denotes algebraic multiplicity. After discarding the zero reducing summand coming from a singular-value expansion, choose the Ringrose basis of \Cref{lem:ringrose-prescribed-diagonal} for any prescribed ordering of the non-zero eigenvalues and complete it through the quotient on which the only spectral value is \(0\). If \(A=[a_{ij}]\) is the Schur matrix of \(T\) in this completed basis, then \(a_{ij}=0\) for every \(i<j\). In particular, equality in the trace lower bound eliminates Schur entries inside the non-zero root-space flag, inside the zero spectral sector, and across the interface between the two.

title: Schatten triangular equality and entry pinching
label: lem:schatten-triangular-equality-pinching
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), let \(T\in\mathcal S_p(H)\), and choose a Ringrose basis from \Cref{lem:ringrose-prescribed-diagonal}. Write \(A=[a_{ij}]\) and \(d_k=a_{kk}\). Suppose that \[ \sum_{k\ge1}\abs{d_k}^p=\norm{T}_p^p. \] For \(P_N\) the projection onto \(\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_N\}\), put \(A_N=P_NTP_N\) and \[ \Delta_{N,p}:=\norm{A_N}_p^p-\sum_{k=1}^N\abs{d_k}^p. \] Then \(\Delta_{N,p}\ge0\), \(\Delta_{N,p}\to0\), and for every \(1\le i<j\le N\), \[ \left\| \begin{pmatrix}d_i&a_{ij}\\0&d_j\end{pmatrix} \right\|_p^p-\abs{d_i}^p-\abs{d_j}^p \le \Delta_{N,p}. \] Consequently every strict Schur entry \(a_{ij}\), \(i<j\), vanishes.

title: Global trace-norm minimum and minimizer classification in a Fredholm-determinant fiber
label: thm:determinant-fiber-trace-minimality
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy the summability hypothesis of \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation}, and write \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z) :=\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j}. \] Let \(M_{\mathcal D}\) and \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) be the collapsed multiplicity function and its support from \Cref{prop:collapsed-spectral-multiplicities}. If \(T\in \sone(H)\) satisfies \[ \det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \] as a holomorphic germ at \(z=0\), then \[ \|T\|_1 \ge \sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \abs{\lambda}M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) =\sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}. \] The cyclic model \(L_{\mathcal D}\) from \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation} attains equality. Consequently, \[ \inf\bigl\{\|T\|_1:T\in \sone,\ \det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \text{ near }0\bigr\} =\sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}. \] Moreover, equality \[ \|T\|_1 =\sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j} \] holds if and only if \(T\) is normal and there exist a Hilbert space \(H_0\) and a unitary \(U:H\to H_0\oplus H_{\mathcal D}\) such that \[ UTU^{-1}=0_{H_0}\oplus L_{\mathcal D}. \] Thus the canonical cyclic model is the entire trace-norm minimizer class in the full determinant fiber, not only in the normal category.

title: Schur-entry stability for trace-norm near-minimizers
label: cor:schur-entry-stability
statement: Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:determinant-fiber-trace-minimality}, let \(T\in\sone(H)\) satisfy \[ \det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \] near \(0\), and put \[ \tau_{\mathcal D} :=\sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \abs{\lambda}M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda). \] Choose a Ringrose basis from \Cref{lem:ringrose-prescribed-diagonal} whose diagonal has non-zero subsequence equal to the determinant-forced algebraic eigenvalue multiset, with the remaining zero entries in the unspecified positions supplied by the triangularisation. Write \(A=[a_{ij}]\) for the resulting upper triangular matrix. For \(P_N\) the projection onto \(\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_N\}\), set \[ \delta_N(T):=\|P_NTP_N\|_1-\sum_{k=1}^N\abs{a_{kk}}. \] Then \(\delta_N(T)\ge0\), \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\delta_N(T) \le \|T\|_1-\tau_{\mathcal D}, \] and for every \(1\le i<j\le N\), \[ \abs{a_{ij}}^2 \le 2\|P_NTP_N\|_1\,\delta_N(T). \] In particular, if \(\|T\|_1\le\tau_{\mathcal D}+\varepsilon\), then for each fixed \(i<j\), \[ \abs{a_{ij}} \le \sqrt{2(\tau_{\mathcal D}+\varepsilon)\varepsilon} \qquad(\varepsilon\downarrow0 \text{ along any near-minimizing family}). \] This fixed-entry conclusion is the maximal consequence asserted without extra tail data: converting it into trace-distance convergence requires a chosen finite window and explicit control of the omitted diagonal and compression tails.

title: Finite chosen-Schur-window distance bound
label: prop:finite-chosen-schur-window-distance-bound
statement: Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:determinant-fiber-trace-minimality}, let \(T\in\sone(H)\) satisfy \[ \det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \] near \(0\). Choose a Ringrose basis as in \Cref{lem:ringrose-prescribed-diagonal}, write \(A=[a_{ij}]\), let \(P_N\) be the projection onto the first \(N\) basis vectors, and put \[ A_N=P_NTP_N, \qquad D_N=\operatorname{diag}(a_{11},\ldots,a_{NN}), \] on \(P_NH\). With \[ \delta_N(T):=\|A_N\|_1-\sum_{k=1}^N\abs{a_{kk}}, \] one has \[ \|A_N-D_N\|_1 \le N\sqrt{(N-1)\|A_N\|_1\,\delta_N(T)} . \] In particular, if \[ \sum_{k>N}\abs{a_{kk}}\le\eta, \qquad \|T-P_NTP_N\|_1\le\eta, \] and \(\varepsilon:=\|T\|_1-\tau_{\mathcal D}\), then \[ \|A_N-D_N\|_1 \le N\sqrt{(N-1)(\|T\|_1+\eta)(\varepsilon+2\eta)} . \]

title: Finite-dimensional trace stability near the minimizer class
label: thm:finite-dimensional-trace-stability
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy the trace-class summability hypothesis, and let \(M_{\mathcal D}\) and \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) be the collapsed multiplicity function and support from \Cref{prop:collapsed-spectral-multiplicities}. Assume that \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite. Put \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z) :=\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j}, \] and \[ d_{\mathcal D} :=\sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}}M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda), \qquad \tau_{\mathcal D} :=\sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \abs{\lambda}M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda). \] Let \(N\ge d_{\mathcal D}\), and let \(T\in M_N(\CC)\) satisfy \[ \det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z). \] Set \[ \varepsilon(T):=\|T\|_1-\tau_{\mathcal D}. \] Then \(\varepsilon(T)\ge0\). Moreover there is a normal matrix \(S\in M_N(\CC)\), unitarily equivalent to \[ \operatorname{diag}\bigl( \lambda I_{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)}: \lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\bigr)\oplus0_{N-d_{\mathcal D}}, \] such that \[ \|T-S\|_1 \le N\sqrt{(N-1)\|T\|_1\,\varepsilon(T)}. \] In particular, in this fixed finite-dimensional fiber, if \(\|T\|_1\le\tau_{\mathcal D}+\varepsilon\), then \[ \operatorname{dist}_1(T,\mathcal M_{\mathcal D,N}) \le N\sqrt{(N-1)(\tau_{\mathcal D}+\varepsilon)\varepsilon}, \] where \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal D,N}\) denotes the above unitary orbit of finite-dimensional minimizers with \(N-d_{\mathcal D}\) zero summands. The exponent \(1/2\) cannot be improved uniformly, even when \(N=2\) and the determinant has a non-zero double root; the explicit obstruction is \Cref{prop:two-by-two-square-root-sharpness}.

title: Finite Weyl--Horn body of the determinant fiber
label: def:finite-weyl-horn-body
statement: Assume that \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite. The body \(\operatorname{HWH}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D,N})\) is the fixed-dimensional set defined in the notation block above. No transition maps between the bodies for different values of \(N\) are part of the definition. If \(N>d_{\mathcal D}\), then \(a_{\mathcal D,N}\) contains zeros; products containing a zero factor are zero, and the terminal equality forces \(\prod_i s_i=0\). This terminal product condition is the only place where algebraic zero eigenvalues constrain the number of zero singular values: the theorem does not delete zero coordinates, nor does it impose a fixed-rank match between zero eigenvalues and zero singular values. The zero coordinates are governed by the zero-inclusive finite Horn theorem recorded in \Cref{lem:zero-inclusive-finite-horn-theorem}, not by an additional cross-dimensional convention.

title: Classical zero-inclusive finite Horn--Li--Mathias theorem
label: lem:zero-inclusive-finite-horn-theorem
statement: Let \(\mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N)\in\CC^N\), let \(b_1\ge\cdots\ge b_N\ge0\) be the decreasing rearrangement of \((\abs{\mu_i})_{i=1}^N\), and let \(s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_N\ge0\). There exists an \(N\times N\) complex matrix with eigenvalues \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N\), counted with algebraic multiplicity, and singular values \(s_1,\ldots,s_N\), all in these fixed length-\(N\) lists and without deleting zero entries, if and only if \[ \prod_{i=1}^k b_i \le \prod_{i=1}^k s_i \qquad (1\le k\le N), \qquad \prod_{i=1}^N b_i= \prod_{i=1}^N s_i . \] The products are interpreted in \([0,\infty)\), so a product containing a zero factor is zero. This is the cited finite-dimensional Horn--Li--Mathias interface used below: the statement includes rank-deficient matrices, zero eigenvalues, and zero singular values, and it is not obtained in this paper by deleting the zero coordinates. In the cited finite theorem, the eigenvalue list is an arbitrary list in \(\CC^N\) and the singular-value list is a non-negative list \(\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_N\ge0\), so zero entries are part of the theorem's hypotheses rather than a limiting or deletion convention. In particular, algebraic zero eigenvalues do not by themselves prescribe how many singular values vanish; they affect the singular-value list only through the Horn inequalities and the terminal product condition.

title: Zero-inclusive log-majorization implies Fan dominance
label: lem:zero-inclusive-log-majorization-fan-dominance
statement: Let \(x_1\ge\cdots\ge x_N\ge0\) and \(y_1\ge\cdots\ge y_N\ge0\). Suppose that \[ \prod_{i=1}^k x_i\le \prod_{i=1}^k y_i \qquad (1\le k\le N), \] where products containing zero are interpreted as zero. Then \(x\prec_w y\), that is, \[ \sum_{i=1}^k x_i\le \sum_{i=1}^k y_i \qquad (1\le k\le N). \] Consequently \(\Phi(x)\le\Phi(y)\) for every symmetric gauge norm \(\Phi\) on \(\RR^N\).

title: Finite-dimensional Weyl--Horn consequence of a determinant fiber
label: thm:finite-dimensional-weyl-horn-cyclic-determinant-fiber
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy the trace-class summability hypothesis, and assume that \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite. This is the fixed-dimensional matrix-geometric consequence of the collapsed trace-class Fredholm determinant data; it is not a separate infinite-dimensional spectral-domain classification. Put \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z)=\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j}. \] Since \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite and the trace-class budget is finite, \(d_{\mathcal D}<\infty\) and \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z) =\prod_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} (1-\lambda z)^{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)} \] by the collapsed determinant identity. Let \(N\ge d_{\mathcal D}\), and let \(s=(s_1,\ldots,s_N)\) satisfy \(s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_N\ge0\). Then the following are equivalent. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item There exists \(T\in M_N(\CC)\) such that \[ \det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \] and the singular values of \(T\), listed decreasingly, are \(s_1, \ldots,s_N\). \item \(s\in\operatorname{HWH}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D,N})\), equivalently \[ \prod_{i=1}^k a_i\le \prod_{i=1}^k s_i \qquad(1\le k\le N), \] and equality holds for \(k=N\). \end{enumerate} Thus the singular-value image of the fixed finite-dimensional determinant fiber is exactly the Weyl--Horn body determined by the collapsed multiset \(M_{\mathcal D}\), with the ambient zero padding dictated only by \(N\).

title: Fixed-dimensional Horn body from trace-class rigidity
label: prop:finite-horn-subordinate-trace-chain
statement: Let \(\mathcal D\) and \(N\) satisfy the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:finite-dimensional-weyl-horn-cyclic-determinant-fiber}. Then the finite-dimensional Horn body and all fixed-dimensional Schatten-budget ranges in the Weyl--Horn theorem, the symmetric-gauge minimization corollary, and the fixed-dimensional Schatten-budget corollary are determined solely by the same collapsed multiplicity function \(M_{\mathcal D}\) that appears in the trace-class Fredholm minimization theorem \Cref{thm:determinant-fiber-trace-minimality}. More precisely, if \(\mathcal D'\) is any other trace-class cyclic datum with finite collapsed support and \[ M_{\mathcal D'}(\lambda)=M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) \qquad(\lambda\ne0), \] then for every \(N\ge d_{\mathcal D}=d_{\mathcal D'}\) one has \[ \operatorname{HWH}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D,N}) = \operatorname{HWH}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D',N}), \qquad a_{\mathcal D,N}=a_{\mathcal D',N}, \] after the harmless ordering convention for the zero-padded lists. Hence the finite matrix consequences add the Horn--Li--Mathias singular-value geography over the determinant-forced finite skeleton; they introduce no invariant beyond the trace-class Fredholm determinant skeleton \((\Sigma,M)\).

title: Universal finite-dimensional symmetric-gauge minimization
label: cor:universal-finite-dimensional-symmetric-gauge-minimization
statement: Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:finite-dimensional-weyl-horn-cyclic-determinant-fiber}, let \(\Phi\) be a symmetric gauge norm on \(\RR^N\), and let \(\|A\|_\Phi=\Phi(s(A))\) be the associated unitarily invariant norm on \(M_N(\CC)\). Then \[ \min\{\|T\|_\Phi:T\in M_N(\CC),\ \det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z)\} =\Phi(a_{\mathcal D,N}). \] The minimum is attained by the normal diagonal cyclic model with diagonal multiset \(\Lambda_{\mathcal D,N}\). In particular, for every \(1\le p<\infty\), \[ \min \|T\|_p^p= \sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \abs\lambda^p M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda). \] Equality cases for the trace norm are exactly those of the trace-minimizer rigidity theorems cited below. The corollary does not assert an equality-class classification for an arbitrary symmetric gauge unless that gauge has an additional strictness hypothesis forcing equality in the relevant weak-majorization inequality; see \Cref{cor:finite-dimensional-gauge-minimizer-taxonomy} for the precise taxonomy used here.

title: Finite-dimensional gauge minimizer taxonomy
label: cor:finite-dimensional-gauge-minimizer-taxonomy
statement: In the setting of \Cref{cor:universal-finite-dimensional-symmetric-gauge-minimization}, the following equality statements are exactly the ones used in this paper. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item For an arbitrary symmetric gauge norm \(\Phi\), the displayed minimum is attained by the normal diagonal cyclic model, and no uniqueness or orbit classification of all \(\Phi\)-minimizers is asserted. \item For the trace norm \(\Phi(x)=\sum_i\abs{x_i}\), every minimizer is unitarily equivalent to the zero-padded normal cyclic model. \item For a Schatten norm \(\Phi(x)=(\sum_i\abs{x_i}^p)^{1/p}\) with \(1<p<\infty\), every minimizer in the finite-dimensional determinant fiber is unitarily equivalent to the zero-padded normal cyclic model. \end{enumerate} Thus non-strict gauges provide attainment only. The trace norm and strictly convex Schatten cases provide the needed rigidity.

title: Exact fixed-dimensional Schatten budget range
label: cor:exact-fixed-dimensional-schatten-budget-range
statement: Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:finite-dimensional-weyl-horn-cyclic-determinant-fiber}, fix \(1\le p<\infty\). The set of all attainable \(p\)-Schatten budgets in the fixed \(N\)-dimensional determinant fiber is \[ \left\{ \sum_{i=1}^N s_i^p: s\in\operatorname{HWH}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D,N}) \right\}. \] Its minimum is \[ \tau_{\mathcal D,p}:= \sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \abs\lambda^p M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda). \] Under the stated hypotheses the zero-padded normal diagonal model makes the fixed-dimensional fiber non-empty. If one discusses a fixed dimension outside these hypotheses, an empty determinant fiber has empty budget range. In the non-empty case with \(N=1\), including the determinant-one zero-support fiber, this range is the singleton \(\{\tau_{\mathcal D,p}\}\). If it is non-empty and \(N\ge2\), the range is unbounded above. Thus, inside a fixed ambient dimension, the only bounded non-empty cases are the one-dimensional determinant fibers.

title: Horn-boundary interpretation of finite trace stability
label: cor:horn-boundary-trace-stability
statement: Let \(\mathcal D\) and \(N\) satisfy the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:finite-dimensional-weyl-horn-cyclic-determinant-fiber}, and let \(a_{\mathcal D,N}\) be the decreasing modulus vector of the determinant-forced eigenvalue list \(\Lambda_{\mathcal D,N}\). Then \(a_{\mathcal D,N}\) is the trace-minimising boundary point of the finite Horn body: \[ \sum_{i=1}^N a_{\mathcal D,N,i} \le \sum_{i=1}^N s_i \qquad \bigl(s\in\operatorname{HWH}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D,N})\bigr). \] Moreover \Cref{thm:finite-dimensional-trace-stability} is exactly the operator-level lift of this scalar boundary statement: if \(T\in M_N(\CC)\) lies in the determinant fiber and \(s(T)\in\operatorname{HWH}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D,N})\) is its singular-value list, then the Horn boundary excess \[ \sum_{i=1}^N s_i(T)- \sum_{i=1}^N a_{\mathcal D,N,i} \] is the trace defect \(\varepsilon(T)\) in \Cref{thm:finite-dimensional-trace-stability}, and that theorem gives trace-distance control of \(T\) from the normal minimizer orbit with square-root modulus in this excess. The exponent \(1/2\) is sharp already along a two-dimensional Horn-boundary tangent direction, as proved in \Cref{prop:two-by-two-square-root-sharpness}.

title: Two-by-two square-root sharpness
label: prop:two-by-two-square-root-sharpness
statement: Fix \(\lambda\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\). For \(c\in\CC\), set \[ A_c=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&c\\0&\lambda\end{pmatrix}. \] Then each \(A_c\) lies in the determinant fiber \[ \det(I-zA_c)=(1-\lambda z)^2, \] whose two-dimensional minimizer class is \(\{\lambda I_2\}\), and \[ \|A_c\|_1-2\abs\lambda = \frac{\abs c^2} {\sqrt{4\abs{\lambda}^2+\abs c^2}+2\abs{\lambda}} =\frac{\abs c^2}{4\abs\lambda}+O(\abs c^4). \] Moreover \[ \operatorname{dist}_1(A_c,\{\lambda I_2\})=\abs c. \] Hence no estimate \(\operatorname{dist}_1(T,\mathcal M)=O(\varepsilon(T)^\alpha)\), with \(\alpha>1/2\), can hold uniformly near the minimizer class in finite-dimensional determinant fibers.

title: Collapsed multiplicities under a Schatten budget
label: lem:schatten-collapsed-multiplicities
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), and let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ n_j,m_j\in\NN,\qquad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\},\qquad \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty . \] Define \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) :=\sum_{\{j\in J:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}}m_j, \qquad \Sigma_{\mathcal D} :=\{\lambda\neq0:M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\neq0\}. \] Then each \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\) is finite, \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is countable, and \[ \sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \abs{\lambda}^pM_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) =\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}. \] Moreover the non-zero eigenvalue multiset of the cyclic \(\mathcal S_p\)-model \(L_{\mathcal D}\) is exactly the multiset in which \(\lambda\) occurs with multiplicity \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\). Thus \(\tau_{\mathcal D,p}\) is the prescribed cyclic-product budget attached to \(\mathcal D\), not a quantity determined by equality of a regularized determinant throughout the full natural \(\det_r\)-domain alone.

title: Prescribed-budget cyclic-product \(\mathcal S_p\)-fiber rigidity
label: thm:schatten-determinant-fiber-minimality
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ \tau_{\mathcal D,p} :=\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty . \] This is the Schatten analogue only after both the cyclic regularized product and the \(\mathcal S_p\) budget have been prescribed. Choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\), and let \(L_{\mathcal D}\) be the cyclic \(\mathcal S_p\)-model from \Cref{thm:schatten-cyclic-model-membership}. Define the prescribed cyclic-product \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget fiber attached to \(\mathcal D\) by \[ \mathfrak F_{p,\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{cyc}}(H) := \{T\in\mathcal S_p(H): \det_r(I-zT)=\det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal D}) \text{ as entire functions}\}. \] All assertions of this theorem are assertions inside this prescribed fiber: the cyclic product, the collapsed non-zero eigenvalue multiset encoded by \(\mathcal D\), and the finite \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget are part of the input. In particular the statement is not made on the full natural \(\mathcal S_r\)-domain of \(\det_r\). If \(T\in\mathfrak F_{p,\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{cyc}}(H)\), then \[ \|T\|_p^p\ge \tau_{\mathcal D,p}. \] Equality holds if and only if \(T\) is normal and there exist a Hilbert space \(H_0\) and a unitary \(U:H\to H_0\oplus H_{\mathcal D}\) such that \[ UTU^{-1}=0_{H_0}\oplus L_{\mathcal D}. \] Thus the cyclic model is the unique \(\mathcal S_p\)-norm minimizer class in the prescribed cyclic-product \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget regularized determinant problem, namely the prescribed part in which the non-zero eigenvalue multiset is the collapsed multiset forced by \(\mathcal D\). As in \Cref{prop:regularized-domain-boundary}, this is not a classification of the full natural \(\mathcal S_r\)-domain of \(\det_r\), nor of the full \(\det_r\)-fiber without the explicit prescribed cyclic-product and \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget restrictions. More quantitatively, let \(M_{\mathcal D}\) and \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) be the collapsed multiplicity function and its support from \Cref{lem:schatten-collapsed-multiplicities}. Choose a Ringrose basis from \Cref{lem:ringrose-prescribed-diagonal} whose diagonal has non-zero subsequence equal to the prescribed algebraic eigenvalue multiset, and whose remaining zero entries occupy only the positions supplied by that triangularisation. Write \(A=[a_{ij}]\). For \(P_N\) the projection onto \(\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_N\}\), set \[ \Delta_{N,p}(T) :=\|P_NTP_N\|_p^p-\sum_{k=1}^N\abs{a_{kk}}^p . \] Then \(\Delta_{N,p}(T)\ge0\), \[ \limsup_{N\to\infty}\Delta_{N,p}(T) \le \|T\|_p^p-\tau_{\mathcal D,p}, \] and for every \(1\le i<j\le N\), \[ \left\| \begin{pmatrix} a_{ii} & a_{ij}\\ 0 & a_{jj} \end{pmatrix} \right\|_p^p-\abs{a_{ii}}^p-\abs{a_{jj}}^p \le \Delta_{N,p}(T). \] Consequently, along any family in this prescribed cyclic-product \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget regularized determinant fiber with \(\|T\|_p^p\downarrow\tau_{\mathcal D,p}\), every fixed Schur off-diagonal entry tends to \(0\).

title: Forced finite budget for prescribed regularized cyclic products
label: thm:schatten-forced-prescribed-budget-obstruction
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be countable cyclic data, with no summability hypothesis imposed in advance. Assume that there is an operator \(T\in\mathcal S_p(H)\) such that the finite-subset regularized cyclic products \[ \prod_{j\in F} (1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j} \exp\!\left( m_j\sum_{1\le q\le (r-1)/n_j} \frac{\beta_j^qz^{qn_j}}{q} \right), \qquad F\Subset J, \] converge locally uniformly on \(\CC\) to \(\det_r(I-zT)\). Then the prescribed \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget is automatically finite and forced by \(T\): \[ \tau_{\mathcal D,p} :=\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j} \le \|T\|_p^p<\infty . \] Consequently the cyclic model \(L_{\mathcal D}\) belongs to \(\mathcal S_p\), the same product is exactly \(\det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal D})\), and \(T\in\mathfrak F_{p,\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{cyc}}(H) \) in the sense of \Cref{thm:schatten-determinant-fiber-minimality}. If the forced budget is sharp, \(\|T\|_p^p=\tau_{\mathcal D,p}\), then \(T\) is normal and is unitarily equivalent to \(0_{H_0}\oplus L_{\mathcal D}\) for some Hilbert space \(H_0\). Thus the obstruction to an unrestricted Schatten analogue is intrinsic: an \(\mathcal S_p\) operator carrying a prescribed regularized cyclic product must already pay the cyclic-product budget, and the rigidity theorem applies only after this finite budget has been forced or prescribed.

title: Finite Schur freezing in Schatten fibers
label: cor:prescribed-schatten-finite-skeleton-freezing
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D\) satisfy the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:schatten-determinant-fiber-minimality}. Let \(T\in\mathfrak F_{p,\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{cyc}}(H)\), choose a Ringrose basis as in \Cref{thm:schatten-determinant-fiber-minimality}, and write its upper triangular matrix as \(A=[a_{ij}]\). Put \[ \varepsilon_p(T):=\|T\|_p^p-\tau_{\mathcal D,p}. \] Fix \(N\ge2\), a number \(R\ge\|T\|_p\), and a finite set \(E\subset\CC\) containing \(a_{11},\ldots,a_{NN}\). If \(D_N=\operatorname{diag}(a_{11},\ldots,a_{NN})\) and \(A_N=[a_{ij}]_{1\le i,j\le N}\), then \[ \|A_N-D_N\|_p \le N^{\max\{1/p-1/2,0\}} \sqrt{\frac{N(N-1)}{2}}\, \Theta_{p,E,R}\bigl(\varepsilon_p(T)\bigr), \] where \(\Theta_{p,E,R}\) is the inverse two-by-two pinching modulus from \Cref{lem:uniform-two-by-two-schatten-modulus}. Consequently, for any family in the same prescribed cyclic-product \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget fiber with \(\|T_\nu\|_p\le R\), \(\varepsilon_p(T_\nu)\to0\), and first \(N\) Schur diagonal entries contained in one fixed finite set \(E\), the whole strict upper triangular \(N\times N\) Schur skeleton tends to zero in \(\mathcal S_p\)-norm.

title: Exact scope of the prescribed Schatten theorem chain
label: prop:prescribed-schatten-chain-scope
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D\) satisfy the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:schatten-determinant-fiber-minimality}. Define the prescribed cyclic-product budget fiber \[ \mathfrak F_{p,\mathcal D} :=\{T\in\mathcal S_p: \det_r(I-zT)=\det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal D}) \text{ as entire functions}\}. \] Then the following finite-budget alternative is exactly the part of the regularized determinant theory proved in this paper; the complementary natural-domain problem is used only as a boundary obstruction. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item On \(\mathfrak F_{p,\mathcal D}\), the non-zero algebraic eigenvalue multiset is the collapsed multiset encoded by \(M_{\mathcal D}\), and \[ \inf_{T\in\mathfrak F_{p,\mathcal D}}\|T\|_p^p = \tau_{\mathcal D,p}. \] The equality class is exactly the zero-padded normal cyclic model from \Cref{thm:schatten-determinant-fiber-minimality}. \Cref{thm:schatten-forced-prescribed-budget-obstruction} also shows that the finiteness of \(\tau_{\mathcal D,p}\) is not cosmetic: every \(\mathcal S_p\) operator whose \(\det_r\) is obtained from the prescribed regularized cyclic product already satisfies \(\tau_{\mathcal D,p}\le\|T\|_p^p\). \item If \(p<r\), the natural \(\mathcal S_r\)-domain of \(\det_r\) contains cyclic models whose \(\det_r\) is defined but whose prescribed \(\mathcal S_p\) budget is infinite. Such models lie outside every finite-budget fiber \(\mathfrak F_{p,\mathcal D}\) of the preceding clause. \end{enumerate} Consequently the Schatten results form a prescribed finite-budget extension of the cyclic construction theorem \Cref{thm:schatten-cyclic-regularized-determinant}, the forced-budget obstruction theorem \Cref{thm:schatten-forced-prescribed-budget-obstruction}, and the minimizer theorem \Cref{thm:schatten-determinant-fiber-minimality}; they are not a classification of all natural-domain \(\det_r\)-fibers. The natural-domain examples are retained only as a scope obstruction: without a prescribed finite \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget there is no lower-bound or equality-rigidity statement of the form proved here.

title: Prescribed-budget boundary for Schatten minimizer rigidity
label: cor:schatten-prescribed-budget-boundary
statement: \Cref{thm:schatten-determinant-fiber-minimality} is a sharp lower-bound and equality-rigidity theorem only in the prescribed cyclic-product \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget fiber \[ \mathfrak F_{p,\mathcal D} :=\{T\in\mathcal S_p: \det_r(I-zT)=\det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal D})\}, \qquad r=\lceil p\rceil . \] It does not extend to a classification of the full natural \(\mathcal S_r\)-domain of \(\det_r\). More precisely, when \(p<r\) there are cyclic data \(\mathcal E\) and a normal cyclic model \(L_{\mathcal E}\in\mathcal S_r\setminus\mathcal S_p\) for which \(\det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal E})\) is defined and has the prescribed cyclic zero divisor, but \(L_{\mathcal E}\notin\mathfrak F_{p,\mathcal E}\) and the \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget \(\sum_jm_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}\) is infinite.

title: Natural \texorpdfstring{\(\det_r\)}{det-r} domain boundary for Schatten budgets
label: prop:schatten-natural-domain-budget-boundary
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal E=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be cyclic data such that \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{r/n_j}<\infty . \] Let \(L_{\mathcal E}\) be the corresponding normal cyclic model in \(\mathcal S_r\), and set \[ \mathfrak G_{r,\mathcal E} :=\{T\in\mathcal S_r: \det_r(I-zT)=\det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal E}) \text{ as entire functions}\}. \] Then \[ L_{\mathcal E}\in\mathfrak G_{r,\mathcal E}, \qquad L_{\mathcal E}\in\mathcal S_p \Longleftrightarrow \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty . \] Consequently, if the displayed \(p\)-budget is infinite, then \(\mathfrak G_{r,\mathcal E}\) contains an operator with no finite \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget. Thus no \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget lower-bound or equality-rigidity statement can hold on all of \(\mathfrak G_{r,\mathcal E}\). In the integral case \(p=r\), this particular domain enlargement disappears; the theorem then concerns the fixed regularized-determinant fiber inside \(\mathcal S_p\), not an additional classification of unrelated \(\det_p\)-fibers. No invariant, minimization principle, or complete list for arbitrary natural-domain \(\det_r\)-fibers is asserted.

title: Finite-dimensional prescribed-budget Schatten stability
label: thm:finite-dimensional-schatten-stability
statement: Let \(1<p<\infty\), put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\), and let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ \tau_{\mathcal D,p} :=\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{p/n_j}<\infty . \] Let \(M_{\mathcal D}\) and \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) be the collapsed multiplicity function and support from \Cref{lem:schatten-collapsed-multiplicities}, and assume that \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite. Put \[ d_{\mathcal D} :=\sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}}M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda). \] Fix \(N\ge d_{\mathcal D}\), and let \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal D,N}^{(p)}\) be the unitary orbit in \(M_N(\CC)\) of \[ \operatorname{diag}\bigl( \lambda I_{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)}: \lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\bigr)\oplus0_{N-d_{\mathcal D}}. \] Put \(E_{\mathcal D}:=\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\cup\{0\}\). For every \(R>\tau_{\mathcal D,p}^{1/p}\) define \[ \omega_{N,p,R,\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{Sch}}(\varepsilon) := N^{\max\{1/p-1/2,0\}} \sqrt{\frac{N(N-1)}{2}}\, \Theta_{p,E_{\mathcal D},R}(\varepsilon), \] where \(\Theta_{p,E_{\mathcal D},R}\) is the two-by-two inverse pinching modulus of \Cref{lem:uniform-two-by-two-schatten-modulus}. Then \(\omega_{N,p,R,\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{Sch}}\) is finite, nondecreasing, and tends to \(0\) at the origin. This is a stability statement inside the finite-dimensional prescribed cyclic-product \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget fiber, not in the full natural \(\mathcal S_r\) domain of \(\det_r\). In particular, the cyclic data \(\mathcal D\) and its \(\mathcal S_p\)-budget are fixed throughout the statement. Every \(T\in M_N(\CC)\) satisfying \[ \det_r(I-zT)=\det_r(I-zL_{\mathcal D}), \qquad \norm{T}_p\le R, \] obeys \[ \dist_p(T,\mathcal M_{\mathcal D,N}^{(p)}) \le \omega_{N,p,R,\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{Sch}} \bigl(\norm{T}_p^p-\tau_{\mathcal D,p}\bigr). \] Thus, in fixed dimension and on bounded \(\mathcal S_p\)-sets, convergence of the regularized determinant-fiber budget to its sharp value forces convergence in \(\mathcal S_p\)-distance to the whole cyclic minimizer orbit with the displayed inverse-pinching modulus.

title: Jordan profiles away from zero
label: thm:nonnormal-jordan-classification
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy the summability hypothesis of \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation}, and let \(L_{\mathcal D}\) be the associated block-cyclic model. Set \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z):=\det(I-zL_{\mathcal D}). \] Let \(M_{\mathcal D}\) and \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) be the collapsed multiplicity function and its support from \Cref{prop:collapsed-spectral-multiplicities}. For each \(\lambda\in \Sigma_{\mathcal D}\), let \[ \pi_\lambda=(r_{\lambda,1},\dots,r_{\lambda,\ell_\lambda}) \] be a finite tuple of positive integers. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item There exists \(T\in \sone(H)\) such that \[ \det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \] near \(z=0\), and for every \(\lambda\in \Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) the restriction of \(T\) to the generalized eigenspace at \(\lambda\) has Jordan block sizes exactly \(\pi_\lambda\). \item For every \(\lambda\in \Sigma_{\mathcal D}\), \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) =\sum_{q=1}^{\ell_\lambda}r_{\lambda,q}. \] \end{enumerate} If these conditions hold, then \[ \inf\Bigl\{\|T\|_1:T\text{ satisfies \textup{(i)}}\Bigr\} =\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}. \] For this fixed profile \((\pi_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}}\), this sharp infimum is attained precisely when every prescribed block has size one, i.e. precisely when \(r_{\lambda,q}=1\) for every \(\lambda\in \Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) and every \(1\le q\le \ell_\lambda\). If the fixed profile contains a nontrivial Jordan block, then the displayed bound is approached by the approximating operators constructed in the proof but is not attained within that fixed profile class.

title: Zero-part freedom in determinant fibers
label: prop:zero-part-freedom-interface
statement: Let \(T\in\sone(H)\). Let \(Q\in\sone(K)\) be quasinilpotent. Then \[ \det(I-z(T\oplus Q))=\det(I-zT) \] as entire functions, and the non-zero Riesz root-space restrictions of \(T\oplus Q\) are canonically the same as those of \(T\). Conversely, suppose \(\mathcal D\) satisfies the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:determinant-fiber-trace-minimality}, the collapsed support \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite, and \(S\in\sone(H_S)\) satisfies \[ \det(I-zS)=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \] near \(0\). Then there are finite-dimensional operators \(S_\lambda\) on spaces of dimension \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\), \(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\), and a trace-class quasinilpotent operator \(Q_S\) such that \(S\) is similar to \[ \left(\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}}S_\lambda\right) \oplus Q_S, \] where each \(S_\lambda-\lambda I\) is nilpotent. The determinant fixes only the dimensions of these non-zero root spaces; the trace-class quasinilpotent zero summand \(Q_S\) is arbitrary and invisible to the determinant.

title: Algebraic partitions are not unitary classes
label: rem:algebraic-partitions-not-unitary-classes
statement: Jordan partitions classify finite-dimensional nilpotent root-space restrictions only up to algebraic similarity. They do not classify them up to unitary equivalence. For example, for \(t\ne0\) put \[ N_t=\begin{pmatrix}0&t\\0&0\end{pmatrix}. \] The matrices \(N_t\) and \(N_s\) have the same Jordan partition \((2)\) whenever \(s,t\ne0\). They are unitarily equivalent only when \(\abs{s}=\abs{t}\), because the non-zero singular value of \(N_t\) is \(\abs{t}\). Thus the algebraic quotient below is classified by partitions, while the stable unitary skeleton retains the full unitary equivalence class of each finite-dimensional nilpotent root-space restriction.

title: Stable unitary and algebraic root-space quotients
label: def:root-space-equivalence-relations
statement: Let \(\mathcal D\) satisfy the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:determinant-fiber-trace-minimality}. For a determinant-fiber element \(T\), put \[ \mathcal R_\lambda(T) :=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\ker((T-\lambda I)^k), \qquad N_\lambda(T):=(T-\lambda I)|_{\mathcal R_\lambda(T)} \] for \(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\). Two fiber elements \(T,T'\) are \emph{stably unitarily equivalent away from zero}, written \(T\sim_{\mathrm u}T'\), if there exist trace-class quasinilpotents \(Q,Q'\) such that \(T\oplus Q\) and \(T'\oplus Q'\) are unitarily equivalent. This is the unitary relation used for the inherited Hilbert-space root-space operators \(N_\lambda(T)\). It records only the non-zero root-space restrictions that survive after adjoining trace-class quasinilpotent zero sectors; it is not a full unitary-orbit classification of the determinant fiber. The added summands \(Q,Q'\) are stabilizing zero-sector noise: their unitary equivalence class, Jordan model, or any finer quasinilpotent structure is intentionally not recorded. When \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite, two fiber elements are \emph{algebraically equivalent modulo the zero quasinilpotent sector}, written \(T\sim_{\mathrm{alg}}T'\), if, for every \(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\), \[ N_\lambda(T)\quad\text{and}\quad N_\lambda(T') \] are similar as nilpotent matrices. Equivalently, after the Riesz decomposition away from zero, trace-class quasinilpotent summands at \(0\) are ignored and only the algebraic \(GL\)-orbits of the non-zero root-space nilpotents are retained. This relation is deliberately not a quotient topology on the full trace-class determinant fiber and is not a unitary equivalence relation; see \Cref{rem:algebraic-partitions-not-unitary-classes} for the separation of algebraic partitions from unitary root-space classes. Thus both \(\sim_{\mathrm u}\) and \(\sim_{\mathrm{alg}}\) classify only data away from zero after adjoining or discarding trace-class quasinilpotent zero-sector summands; they do not classify the invisible zero sector itself.

title: Riesz decomposition with quasinilpotent complement
label: lem:compact-riesz-root-space-quasinilpotent-complement
statement: Let \(T\in\sone(H)\), and let \(F\subset\sigma(T)\setminus\{0\}\) be a finite set containing all non-zero spectral points of \(T\). For \(\lambda\in F\), let \[ \mathcal R_\lambda(T)=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\ker((T-\lambda I)^k) \] be the Riesz root space. Then each \(\mathcal R_\lambda(T)\) is finite-dimensional, and there is a closed \(T\)-invariant subspace \(K_T\) such that \[ H=\left(\bigoplus_{\lambda\in F}\mathcal R_\lambda(T)\right) \dotplus K_T \] algebraically and topologically. With respect to this decomposition, \(T\) is similar to \[ \left(\bigoplus_{\lambda\in F}T|_{\mathcal R_\lambda(T)}\right) \oplus Q_T, \qquad Q_T:=T|_{K_T}, \] where \(Q_T\in\sone(K_T)\) is quasinilpotent. The summands and projections are the standard Riesz spectral summands for compact operators \cite[Chapter~1]{Ringrose1971CompactNonSelfAdjoint}.

title: Quasinilpotent stabilization preserves non-zero root-space invariants
label: thm:quasinilpotent-stabilization-nonzero-invariants
statement: Let \(T\in\sone(H)\), \(T'\in\sone(H')\), and let \(Q\in\sone(K)\), \(Q'\in\sone(K')\) be quasinilpotent. Suppose that there is a unitary \[ U:H\oplus K\longrightarrow H'\oplus K' \] such that \[ U(T\oplus Q)U^{-1}=T'\oplus Q'. \] Then for every \(\lambda\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\) and every \(k\ge1\), \(U\) maps \[ \ker((T-\lambda I)^k)\oplus\{0\} \] unitarily onto \[ \ker((T'-\lambda I)^k)\oplus\{0\}, \] and the restricted root-space operators are unitarily equivalent: \[ U\bigl((T-\lambda I)|_{\ker((T-\lambda I)^k)}\oplus0\bigr)U^{-1} = (T'-\lambda I)|_{\ker((T'-\lambda I)^k)}\oplus0 . \] Consequently the stabilized unitary-equivalence class preserves each nilpotent restriction at non-zero eigenvalues, and therefore also every Jordan block profile. In particular, a determinant-fiber element with a nontrivial block at some \(\lambda\neq0\) cannot become unitarily equivalent to the normal cyclic model \(L_{\mathcal D}\), even after adjoining trace-class quasinilpotent summands at zero. No assertion is made about distinguishing, parametrizing, or classifying those quasinilpotent summands themselves.

title: Stable unitary finite non-zero skeleton under quasinilpotent stabilization
label: thm:stable-nonzero-skeleton-classification
statement: Let \(T\in\sone(H)\), \(T'\in\sone(H')\), and suppose that \[ \det(I-zT)=\det(I-zT') \] as germs at \(0\). For \(\lambda\neq0\), write \[ \mathcal R_\lambda(T) :=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\ker((T-\lambda I)^k), \qquad N_\lambda(T):=(T-\lambda I)|_{\mathcal R_\lambda(T)} . \] Then \(\mathcal R_\lambda(T)\) and \(\mathcal R_\lambda(T')\) are finite-dimensional spaces of the same dimension. If \(T\sim_{\mathrm u}T'\) in the sense of \Cref{def:root-space-equivalence-relations}, then for every \(\lambda\neq0\) the nilpotent root-space restrictions \(N_\lambda(T)\) and \(N_\lambda(T')\), with their inherited Hilbert norms, are unitarily equivalent. For the cyclic determinant fiber over \(D_{\mathcal D}\), this is only a finite non-zero-skeleton statement: after ignoring the trace-class quasinilpotent zero sector, the determinant-forced dimension of the non-zero root space at \(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\). The stable unitary skeleton preserves the full unitary equivalence class of each finite-dimensional nilpotent root-space restriction, but only in the non-zero skeleton just defined. Separately, at the algebraic similarity level, every partition of \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\) occurs as the Jordan profile at \(\lambda\), and different algebraic profiles remain distinct after arbitrary trace-class quasinilpotent stabilization at zero.

title: Finite-support non-zero-skeleton quotient
label: def:finite-support-skeleton-quotient
statement: Assume that \(\mathcal D\) satisfies the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:determinant-fiber-trace-minimality} and that \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite. Write \[ \mathcal F_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{fin}} :=\{T\in\sone(H):\det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \text{ as a germ at }0\}, \] where the Hilbert space \(H\) is allowed to vary. Put \[ \mathcal E_{\mathcal D} :=\prod_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \mathrm{Nil}_{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)}(\CC), \qquad G_{\mathcal D}:= \prod_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} GL(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda),\CC), \] with the product Euclidean topology on the finite-dimensional affine space \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal D}\), and let \(G_{\mathcal D}\) act by componentwise conjugacy. For \(T\in\mathcal F_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{fin}}\), the Riesz root space \(\mathcal R_\lambda(T)\) has dimension \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\). After choosing linear identifications \(\mathcal R_\lambda(T)\cong\CC^{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)}\), the tuple \[ \bigl((T-\lambda I)|_{\mathcal R_\lambda(T)} \bigr)_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \] defines a point of \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal D}/G_{\mathcal D}\); changing the identifications changes the tuple only by the \(G_{\mathcal D}\)-action. This point is denoted \(\operatorname{Skel}_{\mathcal D}(T)\). The algebraic relation \(T\sim_{\mathrm{alg}}T'\) used below means \(\operatorname{Skel}_{\mathcal D}(T)= \operatorname{Skel}_{\mathcal D}(T')\). The topology and closure language on the quotient are always those transported from the finite-dimensional orbit quotient \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal D}/G_{\mathcal D}\). No quotient topology on the full trace-class fiber, no zero-sector invariant, and no unitary quotient, is intended. The equivalence relation deliberately ignores the trace-class quasinilpotent zero sector; it does not classify that sector. In particular, two representatives with different trace-class quasinilpotent complements at \(0\) have the same image in this quotient whenever their finite non-zero skeletons agree; the complements are ignored rather than classified.

title: Finite-support finite non-zero-skeleton quotient after ignoring trace-class quasinilpotents
label: thm:finite-support-quasinilpotent-quotient
statement: Let \(\mathcal D\) satisfy the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:determinant-fiber-trace-minimality}, and assume that \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite. Let \(T\in\sone(H)\) satisfy \[ \det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \] near \(0\). For each \(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\), let \[ \mathcal R_\lambda(T) :=\bigcup_{k\ge1}\ker((T-\lambda I)^k), \qquad T_\lambda:=T|_{\mathcal R_\lambda(T)} . \] Then \[ \dim\mathcal R_\lambda(T)=M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) \qquad(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}), \] and there is a closed \(T\)-invariant subspace \(K_T\) such that \[ H=\left(\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \mathcal R_\lambda(T)\right)\dotplus K_T \] algebraically and topologically, and the restriction \(Q_T:=T|_{K_T}\) is trace-class and quasinilpotent. Consequently \(T\) is similar to \[ \left(\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}}T_\lambda\right) \oplus Q_T . \] Consequently, after ignoring the trace-class quasinilpotent zero summand and retaining only the finite non-zero Riesz skeleton needed in the present theorem chain, the map \[ [T]_{\sim_{\mathrm{alg}}} \longmapsto \bigl([N_\lambda(T)]_{GL(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda),\CC)} \bigr)_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \] is the skeleton map of \Cref{def:finite-support-skeleton-quotient} and is a bijection \[ \mathcal F_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{fin}}/\!\sim_{\mathrm{alg}} \cong \prod_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \mathrm{Nil}_{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)}(\CC)/ GL(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda),\CC), \] where the quotient is the finite-dimensional non-zero-skeleton quotient defined above and \(\mathrm{Nil}_m(\CC)\) denotes nilpotent \(m\times m\) matrices. This bijection records only the finite non-zero skeleton and deliberately discards the trace-class quasinilpotent zero summand; it is not a classification of the full determinant fiber modulo arbitrary quasinilpotent perturbations, and it does not attach an invariant to the discarded zero-sector summand. It is also not a unitary-orbit statement; the algebraic/unitary separation is the one fixed in \Cref{def:root-space-equivalence-relations,rem:algebraic-partitions-not-unitary-classes}. At the Jordan-profile level, the quotient is equivalently the product of the partition sets of \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\). This is an algebraic similarity quotient, not a unitary quotient; the stable unitary relation \(\sim_{\mathrm u}\) preserves the full unitary class described in \Cref{thm:stable-nonzero-skeleton-classification}. These algebraic quotient classes have the same sharp trace-norm infimum \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}, \] and this infimum is attained in a quotient class if and only if all of its non-zero root-space nilpotents are zero.

title: Finite zero-sector invisibility obstruction
label: prop:zero-sector-invisibility-obstruction
statement: Assume the finite-support hypotheses of \Cref{thm:finite-support-quasinilpotent-quotient}. Let \[ S_{\mathcal D}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \lambda I_{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)} \] be the finite non-zero normal skeleton, and let \(N\) be a finite-dimensional nilpotent matrix. Then \[ S_{\mathcal D}\oplus N\in\mathcal F_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{fin}}, \qquad \operatorname{Skel}_{\mathcal D}(S_{\mathcal D}\oplus N) =\operatorname{Skel}_{\mathcal D}(S_{\mathcal D}). \] If \(N\) is non-zero, then \(S_{\mathcal D}\oplus N\) is not similar to \(S_{\mathcal D}\oplus0_{\dim N}\). Thus the quotient of \Cref{thm:finite-support-quasinilpotent-quotient} deliberately forgets a determinant-invisible zero-sector invariant even in finite dimension. This proposition is only a scope obstruction for the finite non-zero skeleton and is not a complete similarity classification of the full trace-class determinant fiber.

title: Classical closure order inside the finite non-zero skeleton
label: lem:finite-support-quotient-closure-order
statement: Assume the finite-support hypotheses of \Cref{thm:finite-support-quasinilpotent-quotient}. For \(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\), let \(\pi_\lambda\) and \(\rho_\lambda\) be partitions of \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\), and let \(\mathcal O_\pi\) and \(\mathcal O_\rho\) be the corresponding finite-dimensional quotient strata, represented by determinant-fiber elements whose Jordan profiles at \(\lambda\) are respectively \(\pi_\lambda\) and \(\rho_\lambda\). Then \[ \mathcal O_\rho\subseteq\overline{\mathcal O_\pi} \] in the finite-dimensional non-zero skeleton if and only if, for every \(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\), \[ \sum_{q=1}^r\rho_{\lambda,q} \le \sum_{q=1}^r\pi_{\lambda,q} \qquad(r\ge1), \] where missing parts are read as \(0\). Thus the quotient closure relation is the product, over the prescribed non-zero eigenvalues, of the usual dominance order on nilpotent Jordan partitions. In particular the diagonal normal minimizer stratum, corresponding to the partitions \((1,\ldots,1)\), is the unique closed stratum in the finite-support quotient, and it lies in the closure of every quotient stratum. The determinant-fiber input here is only the reduction to the finite non-zero skeleton; the closure-order statement itself is the classical finite-dimensional nilpotent-orbit theorem cited below.

label: thm:nonnormal-quotient-degeneration

For each \(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\), fix a nilpotent matrix \(N_\lambda\) on a Hilbert space of dimension \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\), and put \[ J_\lambda:=\lambda I+N_\lambda,\qquad J:= igoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}}J_\lambda . \] Then the similarity class of \(J\) has determinant \(D_{\mathcal D}\) and \[ \inf\{\|SJS^{-1}\|_1:S 	ext{ invertible}\} = 	au_{\mathcal D} := \sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \abs{\lambda}M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda). \] This infimum is attained if and only if every \(N_\lambda=0\).
