title: Nonnormal determinant fibers are trace-norm unbounded
label: cor:nonnormal-fiber-unbounded
statement: Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:determinant-fiber-trace-minimality}, let \[ \tau_{\mathcal D} :=\sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}. \] Then for every \(r>0\) there exists a trace-class nonnormal operator \(T_r\) such that \[ \det(I-zT_r)=D_{\mathcal D}(z) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \|T_r\|_1=\tau_{\mathcal D}+r. \] In particular, the determinant fiber over \(D_{\mathcal D}\) is unbounded in trace norm once nonnormal realisations are allowed.

title: Determinant rigidity by collapsed spectral data
label: thm:cyclic-data-classification
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) and \(\mathcal D'=\{(n_k',\beta_k',m_k')\}_{k\in K}\) satisfy the summability hypothesis of \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation}, and choose roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\) and \((\alpha_k')^{n_k'}=\beta_k'\). Define \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) :=\sum_{\{j\in J:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}} m_j, \qquad M_{\mathcal D'}(\lambda) :=\sum_{\{k\in K:\lambda^{n_k'}=\beta_k'\}} m_k', \] and write \(L_{\mathcal D}\), \(L_{\mathcal D'}\) for the associated cyclic models, and let \[ \Lambda_{\mathcal D} := \bigl\{\!\bigl\{\alpha_j\omega: j\in J,\ \omega^{n_j}=1,\text{ repeated }m_j\text{ times} \bigr\}\!\bigr\}, \] with \(\Lambda_{\mathcal D'}\) defined analogously. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item \(\det(I-zL_{\mathcal D})=\det(I-zL_{\mathcal D'})\) as holomorphic germs at \(z=0\). \item \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)=M_{\mathcal D'}(\lambda)\) for every \(\lambda\in\CC\setminus\{0\}\). \item \(\Lambda_{\mathcal D}=\Lambda_{\mathcal D'}\) as multisets. \item There exist Hilbert spaces \(H_0\), \(H_0'\) and a unitary \(V:H_0\oplus H_{\mathcal D}\to H_0'\oplus H_{\mathcal D'}\) such that \[ V(0_{H_0}\oplus L_{\mathcal D})V^{-1} =0_{H_0'}\oplus L_{\mathcal D'}. \] \end{enumerate} In this situation the determinant germ determines, in the normal trace-class category, a unique block-cyclic realisation class up to zero summands. In particular, \[ \dim \mathsf S(L_{\mathcal D}) =\dim \mathsf S(L_{\mathcal D'}), \] with dimension interpreted as a Hilbert-space dimension. Since \(J\) and \(K\) are countable, this common value lies in \(\NN\cup\{\aleph_0\}\). Separately, \[ \|L_{\mathcal D}\|_1=\|L_{\mathcal D'}\|_1, \qquad \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j} =\sum_{k\in K}m_k'n_k'\abs{\beta_k'}^{1/n_k'}. \]

title: Main trace-class rigidity
label: thm:main-trace-class-rigidity
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be cyclic data with \(n_j,m_j\in\NN\) and \(\beta_j\in\CC^\times\). Interpret \[ \det(I-zT)=\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j} \] in the locally uniform finite-subproduct sense of \Cref{thm:normal-realizability-threshold}. There is a trace-class realisation precisely when \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty . \] At this threshold the determinant determines only the collapsed non-zero spectral multiplicity function \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) =\sum_{\{j:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}}m_j, \qquad \lambda\in\CC^\times, \] and not a finer cyclic Euler-factor packaging. If \(D_{\mathcal D}\) denotes the determinant germ and \[ \mathfrak F(D_{\mathcal D}) =\{T\in\sone:\det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z)\text{ near }0\}, \] then \[ \min_{T\in\mathfrak F(D_{\mathcal D})}\norm T_1 =\tau_{\mathcal D} :=\sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \abs\lambda M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) =\sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}. \] The equality cases are exactly the collapsed normal model class: every choice of roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\) gives a cyclic presentation \[ L_{\mathcal D}= \bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\bigr), \] which is unitarily equivalent to the collapsed diagonal normal operator \[ \mathcal N_{\mathcal D}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \lambda I_{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)} . \] A member \(T\in\mathfrak F(D_{\mathcal D})\) satisfies \(\norm T_1=\tau_{\mathcal D}\) if and only if \(T\) is unitarily equivalent to \(0_{H_0}\oplus \mathcal N_{\mathcal D}\), equivalently to \(0_{H_0}\oplus L_{\mathcal D}\) after the above collapse, for some zero summand. In particular the determinant determines this single collapsed normal model after zero summands, and different summable cyclic presentations of the same determinant germ give unitarily equivalent cyclic models only after passing to the collapsed multiset.

title: Trace-class determinant rigidity hierarchy
label: thm:trace-class-rigidity-consequences
statement: Let \[ \mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J} \] be cyclic data satisfying the summability threshold of \Cref{thm:main-trace-class-rigidity}, and put \(D_{\mathcal D}(z):=\det(I-zL_{\mathcal D})\). The theorem chain has the following hierarchy. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=1.7em] \item The Fredholm determinant germ fixes exactly the collapsed invariant used throughout this section: the multiplicity function \(M_{\mathcal D}\) on \(\CC^\times\), its support \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\), and the sharp trace budget \[ \tau_{\mathcal D} =\sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \abs\lambda M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda). \] It fixes no finer cyclic Euler-factor packaging. \item The full trace-class determinant fiber has the sharp minimum \[ \min\{\norm T_1:T\in\sone, \det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z)\text{ near }0\} =\tau_{\mathcal D}, \] and equality holds precisely for the collapsed normal cyclic model, up to unitary equivalence and zero summands. \item Every downstream package in this section factors through the same invariant \((M_{\mathcal D},\Sigma_{\mathcal D},\tau_{\mathcal D})\): the chosen-Schur stability estimates use only the trace defect above; the fixed-dimensional Weyl--Horn package uses only the zero-padded collapsed eigenvalue vector attached to \(M_{\mathcal D}\); and the finite non-zero skeleton quotient uses only the non-zero root spaces of dimensions \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\). \end{enumerate} Consequently the nonnormal finite-support skeleton, the stability estimates, and the fixed-dimensional Weyl--Horn geometry recorded in the three corollaries below are third-layer consequences of the main trace-class rigidity theorem, not additional classification or minimization layers.

title: Finite non-zero skeleton quotient
label: cor:trace-rigidity-nonnormal-skeleton-package
statement: In the setting of \Cref{thm:trace-class-rigidity-consequences}, assume that \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite. Then the residual nonnormal information modulo trace-class quasinilpotent zero summands is precisely the product of nilpotent Jordan-profile quotients on the non-zero root spaces of dimensions \(M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\), \(\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\). Every such quotient class has sharp trace-norm infimum \(\tau_{\mathcal D}\), and that infimum is attained in the class only for the zero nilpotent profile.

title: Stability with chosen Schur tails
label: cor:trace-rigidity-stability-boundary-package
statement: In the setting of \Cref{thm:trace-class-rigidity-consequences}, the stability results proved in this section are pinching and finite-window consequences of trace minimality. Near-minimal trace defect controls chosen Schur upper-tail entries and, in finite dimension, distance to the normal minimizer class. They do not assert a basis-free global orbit-distance theorem in infinite dimension without the chosen-tail hypotheses.

title: Fixed-dimensional Weyl--Horn image
label: cor:trace-rigidity-finite-horn-package
statement: In the setting of \Cref{thm:trace-class-rigidity-consequences}, assume that \(\Sigma_{\mathcal D}\) is finite and let \(N\ge d_{\mathcal D}:=\sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)\). Then the singular-value image of the finite matrix fiber \[ \{T\in M_N(\CC):\det(I-zT)=D_{\mathcal D}(z)\} \] is exactly \(\operatorname{HWH}(\Lambda_{\mathcal D,N})\). Consequently every unitarily invariant matrix norm is minimized by the normal diagonal model with eigenvalue vector \(\Lambda_{\mathcal D,N}\). This finite matrix geometry depends only on \(M_{\mathcal D}\). For arbitrary symmetric gauges this is an attainment statement only; the equality rigidity used here is restricted to the trace norm and strictly convex Schatten cases of \Cref{cor:finite-dimensional-gauge-minimizer-taxonomy}. For each \(1\le p<\infty\), the exact fixed-dimensional \(p\)-Schatten budget range is the image of this Horn body under \(s\mapsto\sum_i s_i^p\). This is a fixed-\(N\) consequence, not an inverse-limit or stabilization theorem for Horn bodies across dimensions.

title: Determinant-intrinsic trace budget and minimizer class
label: cor:determinant-intrinsic-trace-budget
statement: Let \(\mathcal D\) and \(\mathcal D'\) be summable cyclic data as in \Cref{thm:cyclic-data-classification}. If \[ \det(I-zL_{\mathcal D})=\det(I-zL_{\mathcal D'}) \] as holomorphic germs at \(0\), then the determinant germ fixes the same trace budget in both presentations: \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_jn_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j} = \sum_{k\in K}m_k'n_k'\abs{\beta_k'}^{1/n_k'}. \] Moreover this common number is the infimum of \(\|T\|_1\) over the full trace-class determinant fiber \[ \{\,T\in\sone:\det(I-zT)=\det(I-zL_{\mathcal D})\text{ near }0\,\}, \] and the equality cases are exactly the normal cyclic model class \(0_{H_0}\oplus L_{\mathcal D}\), equivalently \(0_{H_0'}\oplus L_{\mathcal D'}\), up to unitary equivalence and zero summands.

title: Fredholm and regularized zero-divisor correspondence
label: prop:fredholm-regularized-zero-divisor-correspondence
statement: Let \(r\in\NN\). If \(T\in\mathcal S_r(H)\), then \(z\mapsto\det_r(I-zT)\) is an entire function with value \(1\) at \(z=0\), and its zero divisor is \[ \sum_{\lambda\in\sigma(T)\setminus\{0\}} m_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda;T)\,[\lambda^{-1}], \] where \(m_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda;T)\) denotes algebraic multiplicity. Thus the order of the zero at \(z=\lambda^{-1}\) is exactly \(m_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda;T)\), and there are no other zeros. For \(r=1\), this is the ordinary Fredholm determinant; in particular \[ \det(I-zT) =\prod_{\lambda\in\sigma(T)\setminus\{0\}} (1-z\lambda)^{m_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda;T)} \] locally uniformly on compact subsets of \(\CC\). Consequently, if a trace-class operator \(Q\) is quasinilpotent, then \(\det(I-zQ)\equiv1\). If a Schatten-\(r\) operator \(Q\) is quasinilpotent, then \(\det_r(I-zQ)\equiv1\).

title: Classical Fredholm determinant rigidity
label: lem:fredholm-spectral-rigidity
statement: Let \(T_1,T_2\in \sone\). If \[ \det(I-zT_1)=\det(I-zT_2) \] in a neighbourhood of \(z=0\), then the non-zero spectra of \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) coincide with algebraic multiplicity. Consequently, \[ \Tr(T_1^n)=\Tr(T_2^n), \qquad p_n(T_1)=p_n(T_2) \qquad (n\ge 1). \]

title: Product-side divisor multiplicity
label: lem:product-side-cyclic-divisor-multiplicity
statement: Let \[ \mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J} \] be countable cyclic data and define \[ P_F(z):=\prod_{j\in F}(1-\beta_jz^{n_j})^{m_j}, \qquad F\Subset J. \] Suppose \(T\in\sone(H)\) and the net \((P_F)_{F\Subset J}\), directed by inclusion, converges locally uniformly on \(\CC\) to \(\det(I-zT)\). Then, for every \(\lambda\in\CC^\times\), \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) :=\sum_{\{j\in J:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}}m_j \] is finite and is at most the algebraic multiplicity of \(\lambda\) as an eigenvalue of \(T\).

title: Exact trace-class threshold and forced root budget
label: thm:normal-realizability-threshold
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be a countable family with \[ n_j,m_j\in\NN,\qquad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\}. \] For a trace-class operator \(A\), the assertion \[ \det(I-zA)=\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] means the following product-side condition. The finite products \[ P_F(z):=\prod_{j\in F}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j}, \qquad F\Subset J, \] directed by inclusion, converge locally uniformly on compact subsets of \(\CC\) to the Fredholm determinant \(\det(I-zA)\). No summability of the root budget is assumed in this convention; the theorem asserts that such a Fredholm-determinant limit exists exactly in the summable case. The necessity of the numerical bound uses the classical Fredholm zero-divisor correspondence and the Weyl--Ky Fan eigenvalue bound; the theorem combines those inputs into the cyclic-data threshold and records the determinant-forced root budget used by the later minimizer and stability theorems. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item The summability condition \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty \] holds. \item There exist a Hilbert space \(H\) and a normal trace-class operator \(L\in\sone(H)\) such that \[ \det(I-zL)=\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] locally uniformly on compact subsets of \(\CC\). \item There exist a Hilbert space \(H\) and a trace-class operator \(T\in\sone(H)\) such that \[ \det(I-zT)=\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] locally uniformly on compact subsets of \(\CC\). \end{enumerate} Whenever these conditions hold, any choice of roots \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\) produces the cyclic model \(L_{\mathcal D}\) from \Cref{prop:cyclic-data-construction-interface}, and every trace-class realisation \(T\) in \textup{(iii)} satisfies the forced budget inequality \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j} \le \norm{T}_1. \] The cyclic normal model attains this bound.

title: Collapsed-multiset normal realisation and determinant classification
label: thm:collapsed-multiset-normal-realisation
statement: Let \(M:\CC^\times\to\NN\cup\{0\}\) have countable support \[ \Sigma_M:=\{\lambda\in\CC^\times:M(\lambda)\neq0\} \] and satisfy \[ \tau_M:=\sum_{\lambda\in\Sigma_M}\abs{\lambda}M(\lambda)<\infty. \] Put \[ H_M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_M}\CC^{M(\lambda)}, \qquad N_M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_M}\lambda I_{M(\lambda)} \] on \(H_M\). Then \(N_M\) is normal trace class, \[ \norm{N_M}_1=\tau_M, \] and the finite-subset products \[ D_{M,F}(z):=\prod_{\lambda\in F}(1-\lambda z)^{M(\lambda)}, \qquad F\Subset\Sigma_M, \] converge locally uniformly on \(\CC\) to an entire function \[ D_M(z):=\prod_{\lambda\in\Sigma_M}(1-\lambda z)^{M(\lambda)} =\det(I-zN_M). \] Moreover, if \(L\in\sone(H)\) is normal, then \[ \det(I-zL)=D_M(z) \] as a holomorphic germ at \(0\) if and only if there exist a Hilbert space \(H_0\) and a unitary \(U:H\to H_0\oplus H_M\) such that \[ ULU^{-1}=0_{H_0}\oplus N_M . \]

title: Intrinsic normal trace-class realisability criterion
label: cor:arbitrary-collapsed-multiset-normal-realisation
statement: Let \(M:\CC^\times\to\NN\cup\{0\}\) have countable support. Then the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item The collapsed multiset is summable: \[ \sum_{\lambda\in\CC^\times}\abs{\lambda}M(\lambda)<\infty. \] \item There exist a Hilbert space \(H\) and a normal trace-class operator \(N\in\sone(H)\) whose non-zero eigenvalue multiset is exactly \(M\), counted with algebraic multiplicity. \end{enumerate} Whenever these conditions hold, the realisation is unique up to unitary equivalence and arbitrary zero summands, and its Fredholm determinant is \[ D_M(z)=\prod_{\lambda\in\CC^\times}(1-\lambda z)^{M(\lambda)}. \] If \(M=M_{\mathcal D}\) for summable cyclic data \(\mathcal D\), then the cyclic model \(L_{\mathcal D}\) is one concrete presentation of this intrinsic normal realisation; changing the Euler-factor packaging without changing \(M_{\mathcal D}\) does not change the normal trace-class realisation class.

title: Cyclic-block realisation of prescribed cyclic zero divisors and normal classification
label: thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) be a countable family with \[ n_j,m_j\in\NN,\qquad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\}, \] and assume that \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty. \] Choose \(\alpha_j\in\CC\) with \(\alpha_j^{n_j}=\beta_j\), and set \[ H_{\mathcal D} :=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(\CC^{n_j}\otimes\CC^{m_j}\bigr), \qquad L_{\mathcal D} :=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\bigl(C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\bigr). \] Then \(L_{\mathcal D}\in \sone(H_{\mathcal D})\) is normal, and the entire Fredholm determinant \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z):=\det(I-zL_{\mathcal D}) \] satisfies \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z) =\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j} \] locally uniformly on compact subsets of \(\CC\), where the right-hand side is the limit of the positive-exponent finite truncation determinants. On any connected zero-free neighbourhood \(\Omega\ni0\) for \(D_{\mathcal D}\), the reciprocal Euler product is defined by \[ D_{\mathcal D}(z)^{-1} =\prod_{j\in J}(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{-m_j}. \] Let \[ M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda) :=\sum_{\{j:\lambda^{n_j}=\beta_j\}}m_j, \qquad \Sigma_{\mathcal D}:=\{\lambda\in\CC^\times: M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)>0\}. \] Put \[ N_{\mathcal D}:= \bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Sigma_{\mathcal D}} \lambda I_{M_{\mathcal D}(\lambda)} . \] Then \(L_{\mathcal D}\) is unitarily equivalent to \(N_{\mathcal D}\), and this collapsed diagonal model depends only on the determinant germ, not on the chosen cyclic packaging. Moreover, for a normal trace-class operator \(L\in \sone(H)\), the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item The Fredholm determinants agree as holomorphic germs at the origin: \[ \det(I-zL)=D_{\mathcal D}(z). \] \item There exist a Hilbert space \(H_0\) and a unitary operator \(U:H\to H_0\oplus H_{\mathcal D}\) such that, after the above collapsed diagonal identification of \(L_{\mathcal D}\), \[ ULU^{-1}=0_{H_0}\oplus L_{\mathcal D}. \] \end{enumerate} Consequently two summable cyclic presentations with the same collapsed multiplicity function give unitarily equivalent cyclic models after this collapse.

title: A nonnormal obstruction at fixed determinant
label: rem:nonnormal-obstruction-after-realisation
statement: The normality hypothesis in \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation} cannot be removed. Let \((e_n)_{n\ge1}\) be the standard orthonormal basis of \(\ell^2(\NN)\), and define the weighted unilateral shift \[ Qe_n=2^{-n}e_{n+1} \qquad (n\ge1). \] Then \(Q^*Qe_n=4^{-n}e_n\), so the singular values of \(Q\) are \((2^{-n})_{n\ge1}\); in particular, \[ \|Q\|_1=\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}<\infty, \] and therefore \(Q\in \sone\). For \(k\ge1\), \[ Q^k e_n =2^{-(n+(n+1)+\cdots+(n+k-1))}e_{n+k}, \] hence \[ \|Q^k\|^{1/k} \le \sup_{n\ge1} \left(2^{-n}2^{-(n+1)}\cdots2^{-(n+k-1)}\right)^{1/k} =2^{-(k+1)/2}\to0. \] Thus \(r(Q)=0\) and \(\sigma(Q)=\{0\}\). Since \(Q^k e_n\perp e_n\) for every \(k,n\), one has \(\Tr(Q^k)=0\) for all \(k\ge1\), so the Fredholm--Witt expansion gives \[ \det(I-zQ)=1 \] on all of \(\CC\). Consequently, for every summable cyclic datum \(\mathcal D\), \[ \det(I-z(L_{\mathcal D}\oplus Q)) =\det(I-zL_{\mathcal D})\det(I-zQ) =\det(I-zL_{\mathcal D}). \] However, \(L_{\mathcal D}\oplus Q\) is not unitarily equivalent to \(L_{\mathcal D}\oplus0\): the latter operator is normal, whereas \(Q\) is not, and unitary equivalence preserves normality. Thus equality of Fredholm determinants alone does not classify trace-class operators outside the normal category.

title: Block-cyclic normal realisation
label: def:block-cyclic-normal-realisation
statement: A normal operator \(L\in \sone(H)\) satisfying \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation}\textup{(ii)} is called a block-cyclic normal realisation of the Euler data \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\). This definition records only the unitary normal form of the non-zero spectral part. It includes no assertion that \(\Ran L\) is the whole cyclic-block space; that range \(\Ran L\) is the separate object computed in \Cref{lem:cyclic-sum-range-closure}.

title: Algebraic range and closed support of a cyclic direct sum
label: lem:cyclic-sum-range-closure
statement: This lemma uses the support convention of \Cref{def:closed-nonzero-support}: closed support means \(\mathsf S(L)=\overline{\Ran L}\) for normal trace-class \(L\), while the algebraic range itself may be a proper dense subspace. In the notation of \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation}, write \[ H_j:=\CC^{n_j}\otimes\CC^{m_j}, \qquad L_j:=C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}. \] Then \[ \Ran(L_{\mathcal D}) = \left\{ y=\bigoplus_{j\in J}y_j\in H_{\mathcal D}: \sum_{j\in J}\norm{L_j^{-1}y_j}^{2}<\infty \right\}. \] In particular the finite-support algebraic direct sum is contained in \(\Ran(L_{\mathcal D})\), and \[ \overline{\Ran(L_{\mathcal D})}=H_{\mathcal D}. \] If \(J\) is infinite under the trace-class summability hypothesis, then \[ \Ran(L_{\mathcal D}) \subsetneq H_{\mathcal D} =\overline{\Ran(L_{\mathcal D})} =\mathsf S(L_{\mathcal D}). \] Thus the canonical support invariant is \(\overline{\Ran L}\), equivalently the closed span of the non-zero spectral subspaces, and not \(\Ran L\) itself.

title: Support, range, and trace budget of a block-cyclic realisation
label: cor:block-cyclic-rigidity
statement: Let \(L\) be a block-cyclic normal realisation of \(\mathcal D\) in the sense of \Cref{def:block-cyclic-normal-realisation}. Let \(U:H\to H_0\oplus H_{\mathcal D}\) be any unitary representation with \(ULU^{-1}=0_{H_0}\oplus L_{\mathcal D}\), and write \(L_j=C(n_j,\alpha_j)\otimes I_{m_j}\). Then \[ U\,\Ran(L) = \{0\}\oplus \left\{ y=\bigoplus_{j\in J}y_j\in H_{\mathcal D}: \sum_{j\in J}\norm{L_j^{-1}y_j}^{2}<\infty \right\}, \] \[ U\,\mathsf S(L) =U\,\overline{\Ran(L)} =\{0\}\oplus H_{\mathcal D}. \] In particular, \[ \dim\mathsf S(L)=\dim H_{\mathcal D}, \] where this Hilbert-space dimension equals \(N_{\mathcal D}\) if \(J\) is finite and equals \(\aleph_0\) if \(J\) is infinite, and \[ \|L\|_1 =\sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}. \] If \(J\) is finite, then \(U\,\Ran(L)=\{0\}\oplus H_{\mathcal D}\). If \(J\) is infinite, then \(U\,\Ran(L)\subsetneq \{0\}\oplus H_{\mathcal D}\) is a proper dense subspace.

title: Sharpness of the summability condition
label: rem:summability-sharpness
statement: \Cref{thm:normal-realizability-threshold} gives the exact ``if and only if'' statement: \[ \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty \] is exactly the criterion for trace-class realisability of the prescribed Euler data, and hence in particular for trace-class normal realisability. The resulting closed support of the canonical normal model is then forced by \Cref{cor:block-cyclic-rigidity}. Thus the summability hypothesis is not merely sufficient but necessary.

title: Finite Euler products give finite-rank determinant models
label: cor:finite-rank-realisation
statement: If \(J\) is finite in \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation}, then \(L_{\mathcal D}\) is finite-rank. As an immediate specialization, every finite reciprocal Euler product \[ \prod_{j=1}^N(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{-m_j} \] is realised in the determinant-side sense: there is a finite-rank normal operator \(L\) with \[ \det(I-zL)=\prod_{j=1}^N(1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j}, \] and the displayed reciprocal product is \(\det(I-zL)^{-1}\) wherever this determinant is non-zero. The non-zero rank of \(L\) is exactly \(\sum_{j=1}^N m_j n_j\).

title: Connecting Fredholm--Witt identity
label: prop:fredholm-witt-bridge
statement: The following is a direct consequence of the classical Fredholm determinant identity; we record it here to fix notation and to make the Euler-product structure explicit. For every trace-class operator \(T\) and every \(\abs{z}<\min(1,\norm{T}^{-1})\), with the convention \(\norm{0}^{-1}:=\infty\), \[ \det(I-zT)^{-1} =\exp\!\left(\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{a_n(T)}{n}z^n\right) =\prod_{n\ge 1}(1-z^n)^{-p_n(T)}, \] where \(\log(1-z^m)\) denotes the principal branch on \(\abs{z}<1\). This identity holds as an equality of holomorphic germs at \(z=0\); equivalently, it is an identity of formal power series. The exponents \(p_n(T)\) are in general not integers, so the Euler product on the right is not a finite collection of zero-free factors, and the expression should not be extended beyond the common disc of convergence without an explicit branch choice.

title: Arithmetic flexibility
label: rem:witt-arithmetic-flexibility
statement: In the finite-state setting of \Cref{prop:primitive-symbolic-exclusion}, the corresponding coordinates count primitive periodic orbits and are non-negative integers. For a general trace-class operator, the coordinates \(p_n(T)\) need neither be integers nor be non-negative. Thus trace-class realisability is strictly broader than finite-state realisability.

title: Witt coordinates are not cyclic divisor multiplicities
label: rem:witt-versus-cyclic-data
statement: For a trace-class operator \(T\), \Cref{prop:fredholm-witt-bridge} associates the Witt coordinates \[ p_n(T)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)\,\Tr(T^{n/d}) \qquad (n\ge1). \] These are complex numbers extracted from the trace sequence of \(T\). By contrast, the realisation problem in \Cref{sec:fredholm} later fixes discrete cyclic zero-divisor data \[ \mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}, \qquad m_j\in\NN,\ \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\}, \] describing prescribed factors \((1-\beta_j z^{n_j})^{m_j}\) in a Fredholm determinant. In general there is no identification \(p_n(T)=m_n\), nor do the \(p_n(T)\) recover the triples \((n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\). The only overlap is the special integral unit-root case recorded in \Cref{prop:cyclic-witt-compatibility}. Thus the cyclic-block theorem in the next subsection is a theorem about prescribed cyclic zero divisors, not a converse parametrization of arbitrary Witt coordinates.

title: Compatibility of cyclic zero divisors with Witt coordinates
label: prop:cyclic-witt-compatibility
statement: Let \(\mathcal D=\{(n_j,\beta_j,m_j)\}_{j\in J}\) satisfy \[ n_j,m_j\in\NN,\qquad \beta_j\in\CC\setminus\{0\},\qquad \sum_{j\in J}m_j n_j\abs{\beta_j}^{1/n_j}<\infty, \] and let \(L_{\mathcal D}\) be the cyclic model from \Cref{lem:cyclic-product-trace-norm-limit}. Then for every \(n\ge1\), \[ a_n(L_{\mathcal D}) =\sum_{\{j\in J:n_j\mid n\}} n_jm_j\,\beta_j^{n/n_j}, \] and therefore \[ p_n(L_{\mathcal D}) =\frac{1}{n}\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d) \sum_{\{j\in J:n_j\mid n/d\}} n_jm_j\,\beta_j^{(n/d)/n_j}. \] In particular, the Witt coordinates are determined by the cyclic zero-divisor data, but they are generally complex and need not equal the multiplicities \(m_j\). In the special unit-root case \[ \mathcal D=\{(n,1,m_n)\}_{n\ge1}, \qquad \sum_{n\ge1} n\,m_n<\infty, \] one has \[ a_n(L_{\mathcal D})=\sum_{d\mid n} d\,m_d, \qquad p_n(L_{\mathcal D})=m_n. \] Thus the cyclic-block theorem below is a realisation theorem for prescribed cyclic zero divisors; it coincides with the Witt packaging only in this integral unit-root situation.

title: Classical finite-state zeta determinant and Euler product
label: prop:primitive-symbolic-exclusion
statement: Let \(A\) be a finite square matrix with entries in \(\ZZ_{\ge0}\), regarded as the adjacency matrix of a finite directed graph with possible multiple edges; an entry equal to zero means that the corresponding directed edge is absent. Put \(a_n(A)=\Tr(A^n)\), and let \[ p_n(A)=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)\,a_{n/d}(A) \] be the primitive closed-orbit counts. Equivalently, \begin{equation} a_n(A)=\sum_{d\mid n}d\,p_d(A). \end{equation} Then \(p_n(A)\in\ZZ_{\ge0}\) for every \(n\), and \[ \zeta_A(z) :=\exp\!\left(\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{a_n(A)}{n}z^n\right) =\det(I-zA)^{-1} =\prod_{n\ge 1}(1-z^n)^{-p_n(A)} \] as holomorphic germs at \(z=0\); equivalently, as formal power series. If \(\rho(A)>0\), the displayed identity is analytic for \(|z|<\rho(A)^{-1}\).

title: Primitive symbolic Euler data are not trace-class summable
label: cor:primitive-symbolic-summability-exclusion
statement: Let \(A\) be a primitive \(0\)-\(1\) adjacency matrix for a finite one-sided subshift of finite type. Thus multiple edges are not encoded in this corollary. With \(p_n(A)\) as in \Cref{prop:primitive-symbolic-exclusion}, \[ \sum_{n\ge1} n\,p_n(A)<\infty \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad A=[1]. \]

title: Role of the symbolic product
label: rem:symbolic-product-role
statement: For primitive finite matrices, the numbers \(p_n(A)\) are non-negative integers because they count primitive periodic orbits. This arithmetic feature belongs to the finite-state category. The proposition records the classical finite-state determinant/Euler-product identity, while \Cref{cor:primitive-symbolic-summability-exclusion} shows that, except for the one-symbol fixed-point shift, the primitive symbolic Euler product \[ \prod_{n\ge1}(1-z^n)^{-p_n(A)} \] is used in this paper only as a germ-level motivation and not as a summable cyclic zero divisor for \Cref{thm:cyclic-fredholm-realisation}. For instance, for the full \(k\)-shift with \(k\ge2\), \(a_n(A)=k^n\), \(\zeta_A(z)=(1-kz)^{-1}\), and \(\sum_n n\,p_n(A)=\infty\). No twisted orbit, cocycle, or Peter--Weyl refinement of this finite-state product is used below.
